A 10.title: Hydrodynamic model
A 10.text: Selects the governing equations and the numerical grid used for the whole simulation. SFLOW runs on a 2D horizontal grid, FNPF and NHFLOW on a sigma grid, and CFD on the fixed Cartesian grid. The former potential flow solver PTF (A 10 4) has been removed: with A 10 4, the run stops with a message.

A 209.title: Number of smoothing sweeps for the bed
A 209.text: Number of passes of a 1-2-1 type filter (0.5 centre, 0.125 per neighbour) applied to the bed elevation at initialisation. Use 0 to keep the bed exactly as read.

A 210.title: Time scheme for SFLOW momentum equations
A 210.text: Any value other than 2 selects the 3rd-order scheme. The same choice is used for the 6DOF time integration in SFLOW.

A 211.title: Reconstruction scheme for SFLOW momentum equations
A 211.text: SFLOW uses HLL fluxes. This command selects how the face values for the fluxes are reconstructed. The limiters fall back to first order next to dry cells. Options 0–3 also use first-order upwind convection for the turbulence quantities, option 4 WENO.

A 212.title: Turn on diffusion for SFLOW velocities
A 212.text: Needed when a turbulence model (A 260) or the breaking viscosity (A 246 2) should act on the velocities.

A 213.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 214.title: Turn on convection for vertical SFLOW velocity w_s
A 214.text: Only used with the non-hydrostatic pressure schemes (A 220 1–3).

A 215.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 216.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 217.title: Boundary conditions at walls
A 217.text: Ghost-cell treatment of the depth-averaged velocities at solid walls.

A 218.title: Turn on bed roughness
A 218.text: Adds Manning bed friction τ_b/ρ = g n^2 |u| u / h^1/3 with n = k_s^1/6/20. The roughness k_s (m) is taken from B 50.

A 219.title: Additional time step constraint
A 219.text: With option 2, the time step is also limited by the advective Courant number Δ x/|u|, in addition to the default Δ x/(|u|+√(gh)) criterion.

A 220.title: Pressure scheme for SFLOW

options.3: quadratic non-hydrostatic pressure with improved dispersion (A 224)

A 220.text: Option 3 uses the dispersion parameter A 224 and adds an extra time step limit. Option 4 solves the Boussinesq equations in the FUNWAVE-TVD formulation with hydrostatic pressure. Its dispersive terms are explicit, so N 47 is reduced to 0.25 if set higher. Values of 5 and above fall back to option 1. Non-hydrostatic pressure is only solved in wet, deep (A 221) and non-breaking cells (A 242, A 246).

A 221.title: Non-hydrostatic pressure in very shallow regions
A 221.text: With option 0, cells within two or three cells of a dry cell, and cells with water depth ≤ 10·A 244, are excluded from the non-hydrostatic pressure solution. They are treated as hydrostatic. With option 1, all wet cells are included.

A 222.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 223.title: Blending of current and previous free surface for the hydrostatic pressure gradient at patch boundaries
A 223.text: Weight θ of the current free surface: θ η^n+1 + (1-θ) η^n. Used in the hydrostatic pressure gradient at pressure inflow/outflow patches (patchBC). Range 0–1.

A 224.title: Dispersion parameter α for A 220 3
A 224.text: Values below 1.0 are set to 1.0. A value of 1.0 gives the standard quadratic pressure. The default 1.159 is the optimised value. For α > 1, the time step is also limited by the explicit dispersion correction.

A 230.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 240.title: Free surface scheme for SFLOW
A 240.text: Only option 1 is implemented. The free surface solver is created only for values ≥ 1, so do not set this to 0.

A 241.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 242.title: Hydrostatic pressure for shallow areas

options.1: near dry cells and very shallow water
options.2: near dry cells and steep bed slopes

A 242.text: Marks shallow cells as ``breaking'', which switches off the non-hydrostatic pressure there. Option 1 marks cells within two cells of a dry cell and cells with water depth below 0.01 m. Option 2 marks cells within two cells of a dry cell and cells at steep bed slopes (|∂ d/∂ x| > 2, including three neighbours on each side). Option 3 is option 2 plus cells with water depth below 0.02 m.

A 243.title: Wetting and drying algorithm

options.2: depth criterion and wetting from higher wet neighbours

A 243.text: Option 1 decides wet or dry from the water depth threshold A 244 alone. Option 2 also requires a dry cell to have a higher, wet neighbour before it can become wet again. Option 2 helps to maintain mass conservation, e.g.\ in open channel flow. With option 0, the water depth is clipped at A 244 but all cells stay wet.

A 244.title: Absolute wetting-drying threshold
A 244.text: Water depth (m) below which a cell is dry. It is also the minimum depth used in divisions throughout SFLOW.

A 246.title: Breaking wave algorithm

options.2: ON, with slope criterion and breaking viscosity

A 246.text: Breaking cells are treated hydrostatically. A cell breaks when ∂η/∂ t > A 247 ·√(gh). Option 2 also flags cells with free-surface slope |∂η/∂ x| > A 355, and adds the breaking viscosity A 250 in the diffusion terms, which requires A 212 1 or 2.

A 247.title: Breaking wave threshold parameter
A 247.text: Factor α in the onset criterion ∂η/∂ t > α√(gh) (A 246).

A 248.title: Breaking wave persistence algorithm
A 248.text: With option 0, the breaking flag is reset every time step. With option 1, a breaking cell keeps breaking while ∂η/∂ t > A 249 ·√(gh).

A 249.title: Breaking wave persistence parameter
A 249.text: Factor β in the cessation criterion ∂η/∂ t > β√(gh) used with A 248 1.

A 250.title: Breaking wave viscosity
A 250.text: Additional viscosity (m^2/s) added in breaking cells. Only used with A 246 2 and diffusion turned on (A 212 1 or 2).

A 251.title: Initial free surface slope in x-direction
A 251.text: Initialises the free surface as η = -s (x - x_min) with slope s (m/m). Use it, e.g., to start an open channel flow close to equilibrium. Inactive when not given.

A 260.title: Turbulence model
A 260.text: The eddy viscosity acts on the velocities only when diffusion is turned on (A 212).

A 261.title: Length scale factor for the Prandtl length scale model
A 261.text: The mixing length is l = 0.4·A 261· h. Used with A 260 3.

A 262.title: Factor for parabolic eddy-viscosity model
A 262.text: Coefficient α_t of the parabolic eddy-viscosity model (A 260 4).

A 263.title: Factor for eddy-viscosity limiter
A 263.text: In the k-ε model (A 260 1), the eddy viscosity is limited to ν_t ≤ A 263· k/S, where S is the strain rate.

A 264.title: coefficient
A 264.text: Coefficient of the bottom-shear production term in the ε-equation of the depth-averaged k-ε model (A 260 1). Set it explicitly when using A 260 1.

A 270.title: Mesh refinement: number of refined levels
A 270.text: Turns on the mesh refinement with the given number of levels above level 0. In SFLOW, the refinement is only created when at least one of A 273, A 274, A 276 or A 278 is given. When the case is outside the scope of the refinement, a message is printed and the refinement is switched off. SFLOW: A 210 3, A 220 0–4, A 260 0, S 10 0, X 10 0–3, W 90 0. FNPF: A 310 3, A 311 other than 3, A 324 0, A 328 0, A 343 0, A 350 0, A 380 0, X 10 0 or 1. NHFLOW: A 510 2 or 3, A 511 1 or 2, A 512 0, A 520 0–2 (hydrostatic, PJM or pressure correction; not option 3), A 550 0, A 560 0, A 599 0, B 200 0, S 10 0, X 330 0, Z 20 0, and X 10 0–2 (bodies with X 60 1, X 16 0, X 320 0 and A 516 0, 1 or 3). The refinement is also switched off with a message for grid solids as immersed solids (A 580 1), for direct forcing solids (A 581 – A 590), for DEM (E 10 > 0, Section ) and for Lagrangian particles (L 10 > 0). In all models, the grid must have more than one cell in y-direction.

A 271.title: Mesh refinement: regrid interval
A 271.text: Number of time steps between rebuilding the patches from the current refinement flags. In SFLOW, regridding is used with the flow criteria (A 273, A 274) and the body zone (A 278); with boxes only, the patches are static. In FNPF and NHFLOW, regridding is only used with the body zone (A 278), so that the zone follows the body; the patch layout is then kept as long as it covers the flagged tiles with at most 50 % excess. Use 0 for static patches.

A 272.title: Mesh refinement: buffer cells
A 272.text: Number of cells around a cell flagged by A 273 or A 274 that are also refined.

A 273.title: Mesh refinement: free surface jump criterion
A 273.text: A wet cell is refined when the free surface elevation differs by more than this value (m) from that of a wet neighbour cell. Use 0 to turn the criterion off.

A 274.title: Mesh refinement: shoreline criterion
A 274.text: Refines wet cells next to a dry cell, where the water depth is larger than 3·A 244.

A 275.title: Mesh refinement: tile size
A 275.text: Width of the refinement tiles in cells of the refined level. The refined region is made of whole tiles. Values below 4 are set to 4, odd values are increased by one.

A 276.title: Mesh refinement box
A 276.text: Rectangular area (m) that is refined to all A 270 levels. The level-0 cells whose centres lie inside the box are refined.

A 277.title: Box without mesh refinement
A 277.text: Rectangular area (m) where no refinement is created, also when it is flagged by A 273, A 274, A 276 or A 278.

A 278.title: Mesh refinement around the moving body
A 278.text: Refines a margin of this width (m) around the wetted part of the body. Requires a moving body: SFLOW X 10 2 or 3, FNPF X 10 1, NHFLOW X 10 1 or 2. In SFLOW, the zone is aligned with the direction of motion and reaches ahead of the bow by the distance travelled until the next regrid (A 271). In FNPF and NHFLOW (without A 279), the zone is a rectangle aligned with x and y and grown on every side by that distance, suitable for moored and oscillating bodies. In NHFLOW, the hull triangles are refined for the finest level.

A 279.title: Mesh refinement wake wedge
A 279.text: Used with A 278. Adds a wedge with half angle α (deg) that reaches back from the bow by at most L (m), and only as far as the bow has travelled. In NHFLOW, L > 0 also aligns the zone with the direction of motion, as in SFLOW. The default angle is the Kelvin wake angle. Use L = 0 to turn the wedge off.

A 280.title: Mesh refinement: hysteresis
A 280.text: Number of regrids a refined tile is kept after it was last flagged, so that a flag that drops below the threshold for a moment does not remove and rebuild the patch. Range 0–250.

A 281.title: Mesh refinement: vertical refinement
A 281.text: With option 1, every refined level also doubles the number of sigma layers of the level below it. The coarse nodes are nodes of the fine grid.

A 309.title: Number of smoothing sweeps for the bed
A 309.text: Number of passes of a 1-2-1 type filter applied to the bed elevation when the sigma grid is set up. Use 0 to keep the bed unfiltered.

A 310.title: Time scheme for FNPF algorithm
A 310.text: Floating bodies in FNPF and the ice floes (A 380) are advanced within the same Runge-Kutta stages as the free surface.

A 311.title: Spatial discretization for KFSFBC and DFSFBC
A 311.text: Discretization of the horizontal gradients in the free-surface boundary conditions. Options 4 and 5 are the same scheme. The wetting-and-drying version is selected by A 343.

A 312.title: Spatial discretization for second-order derivatives in the sigma coordinate system

A 313.title: Spatial discretization for the bed boundary condition
A 313.text: Discretization of the bed gradients in the Neumann condition for the velocity potential at the bed.

A 314.title: Linear or fully nonlinear free-surface boundary conditions

A 315.title: Free-surface gradient treatment
A 315.text: Option 0 is the legacy scheme: ∂η/∂ x is upwinded by the sign of the potential gradient and used everywhere. Option 1 upwinds the gradient in the kinematic boundary condition by ∂ H/∂η_x, using a symmetric stencil at zero speed. Option 2 is option 1 plus symmetric gradients for the geometry terms (sigma metrics, breaking, wind, dynamic boundary condition).

A 316.title: WENO5 near the shoreline
A 316.text: Only used with wetting-and-drying (A 343 ≥ 1) and WENO5 (A 311 4, 5). Where the stencil is not fully wet, option 1 falls back to a first-order gradient from wet neighbours. Option 0 is the legacy zero gradient.

A 317.title: metrics

options.1: symmetric bed gradient and bed curvature

A 317.text: Option 1 computes a symmetric bed gradient and includes the bed curvature terms. Option 0 is the legacy treatment: a left-biased bed gradient without wetting-drying, and zero bed curvature.

A 318.title: Nonlinear weights of the WENO5 free-surface gradients
A 318.text: Only used with WENO5 (A 311 4, 5), with and without wetting-drying. Option 1 uses the WENO-Z weights with p=2 (Borges et al.\ 2008). Option 2 uses the TENO5 weights (Fu, Hu and Adams 2016): each of the three stencils is either kept with its ideal weight or discarded, depending on the cutoff A 319.

A 319.title: TENO5 cutoff C_T
A 319.text: Used with A 318 2. A stencil is discarded when its normalised smoothness measure falls below C_T. Smaller values discard fewer stencils, i.e.\ the scheme stays closer to the linear upwind-biased scheme. Dimensionless.

A 320.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 321.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 322.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 323.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 324.title: Picard iterations for the Laplace cross-derivative terms
A 324.text: The mixed derivatives 2σ_x ∂^2/∂ x∂σ (and y) of the sigma-transformed Laplace equation are not in the 7-point matrix, but are evaluated on the right-hand side with the current potential. With 0, they are lagged by one Runge-Kutta stage; this error grows with the wave slope. With A 324 >0, the assembly and solve are repeated with the new potential at most A 324 times, until the change is below A 325 times the change of the first solve. Each iteration costs one extra Laplace solve.

A 325.title: Picard convergence criterion for the Laplace equation
A 325.text: Used with A 324 >0. The iterations stop when the maximum change of the potential is below A 325 times the maximum change of the first solve (relative, dimensionless).

A 326.title: Coastline relaxation reference time scale
A 326.text: Only used with the static coastline (A 343 1). If > 0, η and φ in the coastline relaxation zone are relaxed towards their running mean over this time scale (s) instead of towards zero.

A 327.title: Vertical derivative of the potential at the free surface

options.1: Fornberg weights on the sigma nodes

A 327.text: Discretization of the one-sided derivative ∂/∂σ at the free-surface node, used for the vertical velocity in the free-surface boundary conditions. Option 1 computes the stencil weights on the actual positions of the sigma nodes (Fornberg 1988), which is exact for polynomials in σ for any vertical grid stretching. Option 0 is the legacy stencil in grid-index space, which loses accuracy on strongly stretched vertical grids (e.g.\ few layers in deep water with B 103 5). The stencil has 3 nodes for A 311 1, 5 for A 311 2, 4, 5 and 7 for A 311 6, and is reduced next to inactive nodes. Not used with A 311 3 (WENO3), which has its own stencil.

A 328.title: Implicit cross-derivative terms of the Laplace equation
A 328.text: With option 1, the mixed derivatives of the sigma-transformed Laplace equation (see A 324) are assembled into the matrix, giving a 15-point operator (9-point in 2D) instead of the 7-point matrix with the cross terms on the right-hand side. The system is solved with the BiCGStab of REEFMG, preconditioned by a V-cycle on the 7-point part. Only couplings to nodes that are not unknowns (free surface, walls, dry cells) stay on the right-hand side. Requires REEFMG (N 10 1); with other solvers the cross terms stay explicit. Not available with the mesh refinement (A 270).

A 329.title: Order of velocity potential extrapolation for Dirichlet wave generation and active wave absorption

A 330.title: Dynamic wetting-drying: minimum wet time
A 330.text: Minimum number of time steps a rewetted cell stays wet. Used with A 343 2, 3.

A 331.title: Dynamic wetting-drying: rewetting hysteresis
A 331.text: Rewetting margin as a factor of A 344. Used with A 343 2, 3.

A 332.title: Dynamic wetting-drying: width of the front viscosity band
A 332.text: Cells within this many cells of a dry cell get at least the damping viscosity A 346. Requires A 350 1. Use 0 to turn it off. Used with A 343 2, 3.

A 334.title: Wetting-drying: redistribute clamp volume
A 334.text: Redistributes the water volume removed by the wet-dry clamp to wet neighbours. Used with A 343 2, 3, and with A 343 1 if A 337 1.

A 335.title: Dynamic wetting-drying: maximum runup elevation
A 335.text: Maximum bed elevation above the still water level (m) that can become wet. Used with A 343 2. The default sentinel means no limit.

A 336.title: Wetting-drying: one-sided free surface gradients at the front
A 336.text: Computes the free surface gradients at the wet-dry front from wet cells only. Used with A 343 2, 3, and with A 343 1 if A 337 1.

A 337.title: Static coastline: improved treatment

options.2: ON, damping viscosity only in thin-film cells

A 337.text: For A 343 1, option 1 averages the φ clamp over wet cells only and redistributes the clamp volume (A 334). It also uses wet-only free surface gradients with η_xx=0 at the coast (A 336). The damping viscosity A 346 is ramped up towards the coastline inside the coastline relaxation zone (A 341, A 342) and applied in full in thin-film cells (water depth <10·A 344), where a drawdown has exposed the bed. Option 2 is the same, but applies A 346 only in the thin-film cells and leaves the coastline zone undamped (thin coastline). The viscosity requires A 350 1. Option 0 is the legacy treatment.

A 338.title: Remove isolated wet areas
A 338.text: At coastline initialisation, dries out wet areas that are not connected to the main water body.

A 340.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 341.title: Coastline relaxation zone width as factor of the cell size
A 341.text: The width of the relaxation zone along the coastline is A 341 times the horizontal cell size. The value 0.0 means no coastline relaxation zone. A 342 takes priority when set.

A 342.title: Coastline relaxation zone absolute width
A 342.text: Width of the coastline relaxation zone (m). When > 0, it overrides A 341.

A 343.title: Wetting-and-drying
A 343.text: Option 1 keeps the initial coastline fixed and damps η and φ in the coastline relaxation zone (A 341, A 342, A 347). Options 2 and 3 move the wet-dry front dynamically (A 330–A 336). Option 2 uses no coastline damping.

A 344.title: Wetting-drying threshold value
A 344.text: Water depth (m) below which a cell is dry.

A 345.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 346.title: Damping viscosity at the coastline
A 346.text: Viscosity (m^2/s) applied within the coastline relaxation zone, modulated by the relaxation function. With dynamic wetting-drying, it is applied in the front band (A 332). It is applied through the breaking viscosity solve, so it requires A 350 1.

A 348.title: Numerical beach relaxation is used for

A 349.title: Coastline relaxation zone factor for full initialisation
A 349.text: In the first time step of a full-domain wave initialisation (I 30 1), the coastline relaxation zone width (A 341, A 342) is multiplied by this factor.

A 350.title: Breaking wave algorithm
A 350.text: Breaking is modelled with an artificial viscosity (A 365) applied in an implicit damping step. Detection is set by A 351.

A 351.title: Breaking wave detection
A 351.text: Shallow water: ∂η/∂ t > A 354·√(gh). Deep water: free-surface slope > A 355.

A 352.title: Additional filtering for viscosity-based breaking
A 352.text: Filters η and φ in breaking cells for additional robustness (iterations: A 361, A 362), for breaking in:

A 353.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 354.title: Breaking wave threshold parameter shallow water

A 355.title: Breaking wave slope threshold deep water α
A 355.text: Breaking starts where the free-surface slope |∂η/∂ x| exceeds this value. SFLOW also uses it with A 246 2.

A 356.title: Breaking wave slope cessation threshold β
A 356.text: Breaking stops where the slope drops below β·A 355.

A 357.title: Breaking wave viscosity is applied to

A 358.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 361.title: Breaking wave filter algorithm: outer iterations

A 362.title: Breaking wave filter algorithm: inner iterations

A 363.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 366.title: Breaking wave viscosity factor for η
A 366.text: Factor applied to the breaking viscosity when damping η (A 357 1, 3).

A 368.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 370.title: Wind forcing: drag coefficient formulation
A 370.text: Turns on wind forcing in the dynamic free-surface boundary condition and selects the drag coefficient C_d(U_10). Wind speed and direction are set with A 371, the type of forcing with A 373.

A 371.title: U_10, direction
A 371.text: Wind speed at 10 m height (m/s) and the direction it blows towards (deg), measured counter-clockwise from the positive x-axis.

A 372.title: Wind forcing area
A 372.text: Rectangular area (m) where the wind forcing is applied. When not given, the whole domain is forced.

A 373.title: Type of wind forcing
A 373.text: Option 1 gives the wind setup from the surface stress τ=ρ_a C_d U_10^2, spread over the reference depth A 377. Option 2 is deprecated and treated as 1. Option 3 applies a surface pressure in phase with the slope, p_a=βρ_a u_*^2 ∂η/∂ n with β = A 375. Option 4 applies p_a = sρ_a (U_10-c)^2 ∂η/∂ n only on faces steeper than the critical slope (A 376).

A 374.title: Wind decay
A 374.text: Applies a ^2 downwind decay of the pressure forcing over [x_s,x_e]. Requires A 372.

A 375.title: Miles/Plant wind input coefficient β
A 375.text: Used with A 373 3. β≈ 32 reproduces the growth rate of Plant (1982).

A 376.title: Jeffreys parameters
A 376.text: Used with A 373 4: sheltering coefficient s, critical slope, and wave phase speed c (m/s). For c ≤ 0, the celerity of the generated wave is used.

A 377.title: Reference depth for wind setup
A 377.text: Depth h_ref (m) over which the surface stress is spread for A 373 1. For values ≤ 0, the mean still water depth of the forcing area is used.

A 378.title: Low-pass filter passes on the wind forcing slope
A 378.text: Number of 1-2-1 filter passes on the free-surface slope used for A 373 3, 4.

A 380.title: floes
A 380.text: Turns on the ice floes and reads them from the file ice_floes.dat. The file has one entry per line; # starts a comment, lengths are in m and angles in deg:

A 381.title: stiffness α
A 381.text: Stiffness of the compliant lid, k = αρ_w g. The floe follows the rigid-body kinematics up to O(1/α). Larger values stiffen the free surface under the floes and reduce the time step (A 403).

A 382.title: damping ratio ζ
A 382.text: Damping of the lid as a fraction of the critical damping of each floe on the lid spring, c = 2ζ√(kρ_i h).

A 383.title: Ice-water drag coefficient C_d
A 383.text: Skin drag between the floe bottom and the surface flow relative to the floe. Dimensionless. Use 0 to turn it off.

A 384.title: Contact friction and restitution
A 384.text: Coulomb friction coefficient μ and restitution coefficient e of the contacts between floes, obstacles and walls.

A 385.title: Domain boundaries act as walls for the floes
A 385.text: With option 1, the floes are kept inside the domain by contacts with the domain boundaries.

A 386.title: Footprint supersampling
A 386.text: Number of sub-samples per cell direction used to compute the floe coverage φ of each cell.

A 387.title: Floe print interval
A 387.text: Time interval (s) for the floe output. For values <0, the floes are printed with the free-surface print settings (P 180 – P 182).

A 388.title: Contact solver iterations
A 388.text: Number of projected Gauss-Seidel iterations of the non-smooth contact solver.

A 389.title: Footprint edge taper half width
A 389.text: Half width δ of the smooth, area-preserving taper of the floe coverage across the floe edge, in multiples of the mean horizontal cell size. A sharp edge (0) gives a step of the size of the draft in the free surface, which the sigma grid does not tolerate once the floe moves.

A 390.title: breaking

options.1: flexural failure (A 391, A 395, A 397, A 399, A 400)

A 390.text: Bit flags for the breaking mechanisms; add the values to combine them (e.g.\ 7 for all). Contact splitting is only active in 3D. Spalling requires crushing (A 398 >0). The check interval is set with A 394, the minimum piece size with A 393.

A 391.title: Flexural strength σ_f
A 391.text: Flexural strength (Pa) for flexural failure (A 390 1). With A 399, it is the mean of the Weibull distribution for a floe of the reference area.

A 392.title: Contact splitting parameters
A 392.text: Fracture toughness K_IC (Pa m^0.5) and calibration coefficient C of the splitting load F_s = C K_IC h√(D) (A 390 2).

A 393.title: Minimum floe size after breaking D_min
A 393.text: Pieces narrower than D_min (m) are not created. For values ≤ 0, four mean horizontal cell sizes are used.

A 394.title: Breaking check interval
A 394.text: The breaking criteria are checked every A 394 time steps.

A 395.title: Flexural cut lines
A 395.text: Number of cut directions and number of candidate cut positions (beam bins) per direction for flexural failure. In 2D, one direction is used.

A 396.title: Contact force averaging time t_c
A 396.text: Averaging time (s) of the pair contact force that is compared with the splitting load (A 390 2).

A 397.title: Elastic ice properties
A 397.text: Young's modulus E (Pa) and Poisson ratio ν for the flexural stress. For E>0, the bending moment follows from a free-free beam on an elastic foundation with the plate stiffness E h^3/(12(1-ν^2)). For E ≤ 0, rigid-floe statics are used.

A 398.title: crushing strength σ_c
A 398.text: Caps the contact force at σ_c h w (Pa, with the contact width w). The crushing contacts are logged. Required for spalling (A 390 4). Use 0 to turn crushing off.

A 399.title: Weibull flexural strength
A 399.text: Gives each floe a random flexural strength σ_f (A_ref/A_f)^1/m (- u)^1/m/Γ(1+1/m), with the Weibull modulus m, the reference area A_ref (m^2), the floe area A_f, u uniform in (0,1] and σ_f from A 391. For m ≤ 0, all floes have the strength σ_f, without scatter and size effect.

A 400.title: Maximum flexural cracks per floe and check
A 400.text: With values >1, several local stress maxima above the strength can break a floe in one check.

A 401.title: Radial cracks per contact splitting event
A 401.text: Number of cracks, fanned around the contact normal, when a floe splits in contact (A 390 2).

A 402.title: Spalling parameters
A 402.text: Used with A 390 4 and A 398 >0. When the crushed depth reaches the spall length L_sp (m, ≤ 0: floe thickness), the tip of the floe breaks off. Only local chips are created: the chord of the cut must not exceed C_loc times the chip depth. Chips narrower than D_min (A 393) are removed as rubble, whose lid pressure fades out over the time T (s).

A 403.title: time step factor
A 403.text: The lid stiffens the free surface under the floes. The time step is limited to Δ t ≤ A 403/ω_lid, with the frequency ω_lid of the fastest lid-stiffened surface mode on the grid (including the lid damping). A 403 1 is about 60 % of the RK3 stability limit. For values ≤ 0, the previous limit is used: the FNPF time step times 1/√(1+α) (A 381). In addition, the floes do not move more than half a cell per time step.

A 410.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 440.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 509.title: Number of smoothing sweeps for the bed
A 509.text: Number of passes of a 1-2-1 type filter applied to the bed elevation at initialisation. Use 0 to keep the bed unfiltered.

A 510.title: Time scheme for NHFLOW momentum equations
A 510.text: The same choice is used for the 6DOF time integration in NHFLOW.

A 511.title: Flux scheme for NHFLOW momentum equations
A 511.text: Ignored with A 520 3, which uses its own flux scheme.

A 512.title: Diffusion treatment
A 512.text: If used, implicit is recommended. If a turbulence model (A 560 >0) is used, the code sets A 512 2 automatically. The breaking wave viscosity (A 550 1, A 557) only acts with implicit diffusion.

A 513.title: Wall treatment for implicit diffusion
A 513.text: Boundary values used for the implicit diffusion next to solid walls and direct-forcing bodies. Option 1 uses the cell value (zero gradient). Option 2 uses the ghost-cell values.

A 514.title: Reconstruction scheme for NHFLOW momentum equations
A 514.text: With option 4, WENO is used in the horizontal and a limited linear reconstruction in the vertical. Option 5 uses WENO in all three directions.

A 515.title: Free surface treatment at the Dirichlet wave generation boundary

options.1: zero gradient, discharge from the still water depth
options.2: zero gradient, discharge from the actual water depth

A 515.text: Sets the free surface in the inflow ghost cells and the water depth used for the prescribed discharges UH, VH, WH. Options 1, 2 and 4 copy the interior free surface into the ghost cells. Option 1 computes the discharges with the still water depth, option 2 with the actual water depth. Option 3 sets the theoretical wave elevation and water depth in the ghost cells and uses them for the discharges. Option 4 is mass-conservative: the wave kinematics are sampled at the still-water sigma levels and the wave discharge is taken over the still water depth, so that no net second-order (Stokes) mass flux enters the domain. A current is taken over the actual depth, and the ghost-cell velocity is U = UH/D with the actual depth D. For plain Dirichlet generation without absorption (B 98 5 in the input, see B 98), option 4 also imposes the prescribed discharge exactly as the mass flux across the inflow face.

A 516.title: Free surface treatment at forcing object
A 516.text: The free surface is also kept fixed inside the body, as with options 2 and 4, when X 10 4 or X 240 21 is used.

A 519.title: roughness for velocities
A 519.text: Option 1 applies log-law bed friction in the bottom layer, with roughness k_s (m) from B 50, or from the sediment settings if sediment transport is active. Option 2 applies wall-function friction in all cells next to the bed (B 50) and next to solid walls and forcing bodies (B 57), including the vertical velocity.

A 520.title: Pressure scheme for NHFLOW
A 520.text: Option 3 uses its own flux scheme and ignores A 511. Membranes (X 330) require option 1 or 2. With a moving membrane (structure rigid or flexible), option 2 is changed to option 1 automatically. Mesh refinement (A 270) supports options 0–2.

A 521.title: Fluxes at direct-forcing interfaces
A 521.text: With option 0, velocities and fluxes are set to zero on cell faces between fluid cells and direct-forcing solids or floating bodies. Any other value turns this off.

A 522.title: slope factor in the non-hydrostatic pressure
A 522.text: In the bottom layer, the vertical interpolation weight of the horizontal velocities in the pressure solution (A 520 1, 2) is reduced by (1 - A 522 |∂ d/∂ x|, 0). This improves robustness over steep bed slopes.

A 523.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 524.title: Horizontal gradients for the sigma transformation

options.3: van Leer limited, from the filtered free surface

A 524.text: Discretization of the free surface and bed gradients in the sigma coordinate metrics.

A 525.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 526.title: Direct forcing interface width factor
A 526.text: The smoothed direct forcing interface has a width of A 526 times the horizontal cell size. It applies to fixed solids (A 580 1, A 581–A 590) and floating bodies, including porous floating bodies (X 16).

A 527.title: Nonlinear weights of the WENO reconstruction
A 527.text: Only used with the WENO reconstruction (A 514 4, 5), for all reconstructed quantities. Option 1 uses the WENO-Z weights with p=2 (Borges et al.\ 2008). Option 2 uses the TENO5 weights (Fu, Hu and Adams 2016): each of the three stencils is either kept with its ideal weight or discarded, depending on the cutoff A 528.

A 528.title: TENO5 cutoff C_T
A 528.text: Used with A 527 2. A stencil is discarded when its normalised smoothness measure falls below C_T. Smaller values discard fewer stencils, i.e.\ the scheme stays closer to the linear upwind-biased scheme. Dimensionless.

A 531.title: Froude number limiter
A 531.text: Limits the discharge in each wet cell to |uh| ≤ A 531· h√(gh). Next to dry cells, a factor 0.1 is applied when B 60 is used (NHFLOW: B 60 1, also in the shallow cells of A 545). In NHFLOW, the area is set by A 532. Also used by SFLOW.

A 532.title: Froude number limiter area
A 532.text: Option 2 applies the limiter only in shallow cells near dry cells (see A 545).

A 533.title: Vertical velocity time step control
A 533.text: Adds the vertical Courant number Δ z/|w| and a source-term criterion to the time step control.

A 540.title: Wetting-drying scheme

options.1: depth criterion and wetting from higher wet neighbours

A 540.text: Option 1 lets a dry cell become wet only from a higher, wet neighbour, and uses the wet-dry face flux treatment. Option 2 decides wet or dry from the depth threshold A 544 alone.

A 541.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 542.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 543.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 544.title: Absolute wetting-drying threshold
A 544.text: Water depth (m) below which a cell is dry. It is also the minimum depth used in divisions throughout NHFLOW.

A 545.title: Shallow water criterion factor
A 545.text: Cells with water depth ≤ A 545·A 544, or within two (x-direction) or three (y-direction) cells of a dry cell, are ``not deep''. There, the non-hydrostatic pressure is not solved, and A 532 2 applies the Froude number limiter.

A 550.title: Breaking wave algorithm
A 550.text: Breaking cells are detected with A 551 and receive the viscosity A 557. The viscosity is added in the implicit diffusion, so A 512 2 (or a turbulence model, A 560) is needed for it to act.

A 551.title: Breaking wave detection
A 551.text: Shallow water: ∂η/∂ t > A 554·√(gh). Deep water: free-surface slope > A 555.

A 552.title: Additional filtering for viscosity-based breaking
A 552.text: Filters the water depth in breaking cells for additional robustness, for breaking in:

A 553.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 554.title: Breaking wave threshold parameter shallow water

A 555.title: Breaking wave slope threshold deep water
A 555.text: Breaking starts where the free-surface slope exceeds this value.

A 556.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 560.title: Turbulence model
A 560.text: Any turbulence model switches on implicit diffusion (A 512 2). The URANS variants scale the eddy viscosity with a filter based on the local cell size and coefficient A 568.

A 564.title: Eddy viscosity limiter
A 564.text: Option 1 is the realizability limiter ν_t ≤ T 31· k/S. Option 2 is the SST/Bradshaw limiter ν_t ≤ a_1 k/(F_2 S).

A 565.title: Turbulence model stabilization
A 565.text: Stabilization of the eddy viscosity in nearly potential flow regions, following Larsen and Fuhrman (2018). Uses T 42. Applies to the k-ω and k-ε models.

A 567.title: Free surface boundary condition for turbulent dissipation

options.3: ON, length scaled with water depth (k-ω only)

A 567.text: Sets ε or ω in the top layer from a mixing length based on T 37. For k-ε, the length is T 37· h, and only option 1 has an effect. For k-ω, the length is T 37 (m) with options 1 and 2, and T 37· h with option 3.

A 568.title: URANS filter coefficient
A 568.text: Coefficient of the URANS eddy viscosity filter for A 560 21 and 22.

A 569.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 570.title: Wind forcing: drag coefficient formulation
A 570.text: Turns on wind forcing and selects the drag coefficient C_d(U_10). Wind speed and direction are set with A 571, the type of forcing with A 573.

A 571.title: U_10, direction
A 571.text: Wind speed at 10 m height (m/s) and the direction it blows towards (deg), measured counter-clockwise from the positive x-axis. Also used for the windage of Lagrangian particles if L 41 is not given and A 570 >0.

A 572.title: Wind forcing area
A 572.text: Rectangular area (m) where the wind forcing is applied. When not given, the whole domain is forced.

A 573.title: Type of wind forcing
A 573.text: Option 1 applies the surface shear stress τ=ρ_a C_d U_10^2 in the top sigma layer. Option 2 is deprecated and treated as 1. Options 3 and 4 apply a surface pressure that acts in all layers: Miles/Plant (A 575) or modified Jeffreys (A 576). The slope used for options 3 and 4 is filtered with A 578 passes.

A 574.title: Wind decay
A 574.text: Applies a ^2 downwind decay of the wind forcing over [x_s,x_e] for all forcing types. Requires A 572.

A 575.title: Miles/Plant wind input coefficient β
A 575.text: Used with A 573 3: p_a=βρ_a u_*^2 ∂η/∂ n.

A 576.title: Jeffreys parameters
A 576.text: Used with A 573 4: sheltering coefficient s, critical slope, and wave phase speed c (m/s). For c ≤ 0, the celerity of the generated wave is used.

A 578.title: Low-pass filter passes on the wind forcing slope
A 578.text: Number of 1-2-1 filter passes on the free-surface slope used for A 573 3, 4.

A 580.title: Solids of the grid file

options.0: solids are part of the bed

A 580.text: Treatment of the solid entities (S) of the DIVEMesh grid file (DIVEMesh_Grid/grid-geometry.dat) in NHFLOW. With option 0, the solids raise the bed level. With option 1, they are represented as immersed solids by direct forcing, in the same way as A 581–A 590, and the bed level only follows the topography (T). Option 1 cannot be combined with mesh refinement (A 270).

A 581.title: Direct forcing rectangular box
A 581.text: Fixed solid box (m) represented by direct forcing. It can be given several times.

A 583.title: Direct forcing cylinder in y-direction
A 583.text: Horizontal cylinder along y with centre (x_c, z_c), extent y_s to y_e and radius r (m).

A 584.title: Direct forcing cylinder in z-direction
A 584.text: Vertical cylinder with centre (x_c, y_c), extent z_s to z_e and radius r (m). These cylinders are also used by the DLM method (A 599).

A 585.title: Direct forcing cylinder with flexible orientation
A 585.text: Cylinder or cone between the start and end points (m), with end faces orthogonal to the axis and radii r_s and r_e (m) at the two ends. Suitable, e.g., for jacket members.

A 586.title: Direct forcing sphere
A 586.text: Sphere with centre (x_c, y_c, z_c) and radius r (m).

A 587.title: Direct forcing wedge object in x-direction
A 587.text: Wedge within the given bounding box (m), oriented in x-direction.

A 588.title: Direct forcing wedge object in y-direction
A 588.text: Wedge within the given bounding box (m), oriented in y-direction.

A 589.title: Direct forcing wedge object in z-direction
A 589.text: Wedge within the given bounding box (m), oriented in z-direction.

A 590.title: Direct forcing solid from STL file
A 590.text: Reads the file `solid.stl' and represents the geometry by direct forcing. It can be scaled, translated and rotated with A 591–A 593. IMPORTANT: the STL file needs to be in ASCII format! Most CAD programs export to a binary STL file. It is possible to use e.g. Paraview for STL conversion from binary to ASCII.

A 591.title: Scale STL geometry
A 591.text: Scaling factors in x-, y- and z-direction for the A 590 geometry. They are applied before translation and rotation.

A 592.title: Translate STL geometry
A 592.text: Shift (m) of the A 590 geometry, applied after scaling.

A 593.title: Rotate STL geometry
A 593.text: Rotates the A 590 geometry about the origin (x_o, y_o, z_o) (m) by the angles φ, θ, ψ (deg) about the x-, y- and z-axes. Applied after scaling and translation.

A 594.text: Not in the user guide yet.

A 599.title: the distributed Lagrange multiplier method instead of direct forcing
A 599.text: With option 1, the direct forcing for solids and floating bodies is turned off and the DLM method is used for the A 584 cylinders. The DLM method only supports the A 584 cylinders; other solid objects (A 580, A 581–A 590) and floating bodies are not represented.

B 10.title: Wall functions for the velocities
B 10.text: Applies a logarithmic wall law to the tangential velocities at walls and bottom, using the roughness from B 50–B 56.

B 11.title: Wall functions for the turbulence model
B 11.text: Wall-law boundary conditions for the turbulence quantities (k, ε/ω, eddy viscosity) at walls and bottom in NHFLOW. When OFF, the turbulence quantities are set to zero in the wall ghost cells.

B 20.title: Slip or no-slip boundary conditions for velocities

options.3: no-slip via Dirichlet image-point extrapolation (see B 29)
options.4: no-slip at walls, slip at the bottom topography

B 20.text: Ghost-cell treatment of the velocities at walls and at the bottom topography.

B 21.title: Preserve tangential velocities for forcing
B 21.text: Used by the direct forcing immersed boundary method together with B 20 1 or B 20 2. When ON, the tangential velocities at the solid surface are preserved in the forcing; when OFF, all velocity components inside the solid are simply forced to zero.

B 22.title: Smooth or rough wall law for the bed shear stress
B 22.text: Wall law used to compute the bed shear stress for sediment transport in NHFLOW when S 16 1 is selected. The roughness is the effective bed roughness of the sediment model.

B 23.title: Extrapolation or reflection for ghostcell updates

B 29.title: Image point distance for ghost-cell Dirichlet extrapolation
B 29.text: Distance of the image point from the wall as a fraction γ of the cell size, used by the Dirichlet ghost-cell extrapolation (e.g.\ B 20 3). Range 0 < γ ≤ 1.

B 30.title: Type of pressure reference point

options.2: at the free surface above the inlet: the gage x- and y-location is set automatically to the inlet cell with the smallest x- and y-coordinates (outlet with the largest x-coordinate when B 99 ≥ 3), the z-location follows the free surface
options.3: atmospheric pressure B 31 imposed at the top boundary (lid)
options.4: normalize the pressure so that its mean value at the free surface (zero level set contour) is zero

B 30.text: Defines how the pressure level is fixed. The reference value is given in B 31; how it is applied is set by B 33.

B 31.title: Pressure reference value
B 31.text: Pressure in Pa at the reference point (B 30 1, 2) or at the lid (B 30 3).

B 32.title: Location of the fixed pressure reference point
B 32.text: Coordinates in m, used with B 30 1. If B 32 is not given, the location is set automatically to the inlet cell with the smallest x- and y-coordinates and the highest z-coordinate (outlet with the largest x-coordinate when B 99 ≥ 3). For B 30 2 and 3 the location is always set automatically and B 32 is overwritten.

B 33.title: Type of pressure reference gage normalization
B 33.text: Virtual normalization only stores the gage offset and subtracts it in the output, inline normalization subtracts it from the pressure field in every time step. For certain configurations, inline pressure normalization causes instabilities.

B 50.title: Global wall roughness
B 50.text: Equivalent sand-grain roughness k_s in m, used for the bed and all walls unless overwritten by B 51–B 56 (CFD) or B 57 (NHFLOW side walls). In SFLOW it is the bed roughness used for the bottom friction.

B 51.title: Wall 1 roughness
B 51.text: Roughness k_s in m for the boundary side facing the negative x-direction (x_min). A value ≤ 0 means not set, B 50 is used.

B 52.title: Wall 2 roughness
B 52.text: Roughness k_s in m for the boundary side facing the positive y-direction (y_max).

B 53.title: Wall 3 roughness
B 53.text: Roughness k_s in m for the boundary side facing the negative y-direction (y_min).

B 54.title: Wall 4 roughness
B 54.text: Roughness k_s in m for the boundary side facing the positive x-direction (x_max).

B 55.title: Wall 5 roughness
B 55.text: Roughness k_s in m for the boundary side facing the negative z-direction (bottom).

B 56.title: Wall 6 roughness
B 56.text: Roughness k_s in m for the boundary side facing the positive z-direction (top).

B 57.title: Side wall roughness for NHFLOW
B 57.text: Roughness k_s in m for the side walls, the top and solid bodies in the NHFLOW wall law (velocities with A 519 2, and the k-ω wall boundary conditions). The bottom uses B 50.

B 60.title: Enable ioFlow for open channel flow
B 60.text: This parameter is important for open channel flow calculations. The ioFlow module makes sure that the inflow discharge as given in W 10 is constant throughout the computation even though the inflow water level may change. This is the counterpart to B 90 for open channel flow. When selecting the hydrograph inflow option, make sure that a file with the name ``hydrograph.dat'' is present in the simulation folder. When selecting the hydrograph outflow option, make sure that a file with the name ``hydrograph_out.dat'' is present in the simulation folder. The data format of the hydrograph file consists of two columns, the first one gives the time in s and the second column the discharge in m^3/s.

B 61.title: Inflow profile for ioFlow

options.4: logarithmic profile only for phase 1, bed
options.5: logarithmic profile only for phase 1, sidewalls and bed

B 61.text: Velocity profile at the inflow boundary for B 60. The logarithmic profiles use the roughness B 50. ``Phase 1'' refers to the water phase.

B 71.title: y-origin
B 71.text: Relaxation of the free surface towards a fixed water level for the initialization only (first time step), for open channel flow with B 60. value: water level z-coordinate in m; distance: length of the relaxation zone in m, measured from the line; line angle in deg; x- and y-origin of the line in m. Multiple zones are possible.

B 75.title: Outflow boundary condition

options.3: u-velocity scaled so that the outflow discharge matches the inflow discharge W 10 (scaling limited to 0.1–2.0), convection condition for v and w

B 75.text: Boundary condition for the velocities at the outflow boundary.

B 77.title: Pressure outflow boundary conditions

options.2: controlled outflow with free surface condition (see F 62)

B 77.text: Option 2 controls the outflow water level with F 62. SFLOW only uses option 10.

B 81.title: Focus location and focus time for focused waves
B 81.text: x- and y-location in m and time in s at which the wave components of the focused wave theories (B 92 41–43) are in phase. For a 2D simulation set y_f to 0.0.

B 82.title: Type of focusing amplitude calculation

options.3: Constant wave steepness spectrum, see B 83

B 82.text: Amplitudes A_i of the wave components of focused waves. For NewWave the amplitudes are scaled with the spectrum so that their sum equals half of the wave height given in B 91 or B 93. Options 11–14 are identical to 1–4 but shift all phases by π, so that a wave trough instead of a crest is focused. The phase shift is only applied for unidirectional focused waves (B 130 0).

B 83.title: Gain factor per wave component for constant wave steepness spectrum focused waves
B 83.text: The amplitudes of the wave components are calculated using A_i = (B83)/(k_i) (B 82 3). The frequency distribution is calculated as defined in B 84. For the Gaussian wavepackets (B 85 6) this value is used as the width of the Gaussian distribution in rad/s.

B 85.title: Wave spectrum for irregular waves
B 85.text: For the spectrum file, provide a ``spectrum-file.dat'' with the two columns ``ω'' and ``S''. For the 2D spectrum file, provide a ``spectrum-file-2d.dat'': the header line starts with a label followed by the directions, each following row gives the frequency and the spectral values for each direction; the number of frequencies and directions then replaces B 86 and B 133. The JONSWAP-type spectra use γ from B 88.

B 86.title: Number of regular waves for irregular wave generation
B 86.text: Number of frequency components used to discretise the spectrum. With directional spreading (B 130) the total number of components is B 86 × B 133.

B 87.title: Frequency range for irregular wave generation
B 87.text: Start and end angular frequency in rad/s of the discretised spectrum. When not given, the model will calculate the values automatically.

B 88.title: Peak enhancement factor γ
B 88.text: Used by the JONSWAP, Goda JONSWAP and TMA spectra (B 85 2, 21, 22).

B 89.title: Wave generation optimization through space-time decomposition
B 89.text: Splits the input wave into precomputed spatial and temporal parts, which makes wave generation with many components considerably cheaper. Supported for the wave theories B 92 5, 31, 41 and 51. In CFD it applies to relaxation generation (B 98 2), in FNPF and NHFLOW to relaxation and Dirichlet generation. Not available in SFLOW. Cannot be combined with additional wave sources (B 500) or zone sources (B 524); the program stops with an input error.

B 90.title: Enable ioWave for numerical wave tank
B 90.text: This parameter turns on the numerical wave tank. It is the counterpart to B 60 for wave simulations. A wave tank setup needs at least: the wave theory (B 92), the wave parameters (B 91 or B 93), the wave generation method (B 98), the numerical beach (B 99) and, for relaxation zones, their lengths (B 96).

B 91.title: length
B 91.text: Wave input with the wave length known: H in m and L in m. The wave period is calculated from the dispersion relation of the selected wave theory. For irregular, focused and reconstructed waves (B 92 31–53) the first value is the significant wave height H_s and the second the peak wave length, from which the peak period is calculated with linear dispersion. Use either B 91 or B 93; if both are given, B 93 is used. Exactly two values must be given, otherwise the program stops with an input error.

B 92.title: Wave type

options.20: Piston Wavemaker based on η timeseries
options.24: Flap Wavemaker based on η timeseries
options.61: Hydrodynamic Coupling HDC (FNPF to CFD or SFLOW to CFD)
options.70: Steady Surface Gravity Wave SSGW * (number of Fourier modes B 170)

B 92.text: Different wave theories can be used as input for the numerical wave tank. It is important to check beforehand whether the selected theory fits the given wave conditions consisting of wave height, wave length/wave period (B 91 or B 93) and still water depth (B 94). The table below lists which generation methods (B 98) are available for each theory and model. For the piston and flap wavemaker theories with η timeseries input (20, 24), provide a ``wavemaker_eta.dat'' input file with two columns ``t'' and ``η''. For the piston and flap wavemaker theories (21, 22), provide a ``wavemaker.dat'' input file with two columns ``t'' and ``X'' or ``t'' and ``β'', depending on input from B 116. The vertical extent of the paddle is set with B 110 (piston), B 111 (flap) or B 112 (double-hinged flap). A second-order correction of the paddle signal can be added with B 113 and B 114, and in FNPF the moving-paddle boundary terms with B 119. For the double-hinged flap wavemaker, two ``X'' or two ``β'' columns are expected. For giving two ``X'' columns, this will be the total excitation at the end of each flap. For giving two ``β'' columns, the second angle is the additional excitation of the second fla

B 93.title: period
B 93.text: Wave input with the wave period known: H in m and T in s. The wave length is calculated from the dispersion relation of the selected wave theory. For irregular, focused and reconstructed waves (B 92 31–53) the first value is the significant wave height H_s and the second the peak period T_p. Use either B 91 or B 93; if both are given, B 93 is used. Exactly two values must be given, otherwise the program stops with an input error.

B 94.title: Water depth d for wave theory
B 94.text: Water depth in m used to evaluate the wave theory. If not given, d is set to the still water level F 60, which requires the bed at the wave generation to be located at z=0.0 m.

B 95.text: Not in the user guide yet.

B 96.title: Lengths of the relaxation zones
B 96.text: Length in m of the wave generation relaxation zone (dist1), measured from the start of the domain (x_min), and length in m of the numerical beach relaxation zone (dist2), measured from the end of the domain (x_max). The relaxation zones are only active for relaxation generation (B 98 2) and relaxation beaches (B 99 1 or 2). If B 108 or B 107 are given, they replace the default zones and the respective value of B 96 is not used. A typical choice, used in the tutorials, is a generation zone of about one wavelength and a numerical beach of about two wavelengths, e.g.\ B 96 4.0 8.0 for L = 4.0 m. Exactly two values must be given, otherwise the program stops with an input error.

B 97.title: Waves on a current for NHFLOW

options.0: OFF, beach relaxes the velocity to zero
options.1: ON, beach relaxes the velocity to the inflow current

B 97.text: With B 97 1, the NHFLOW numerical beach relaxation zones (B 99 1 or 2, B 107, B 520 method 2) relax the horizontal velocity towards the inflow current velocity U_i = W 10 / inflow cross-section area (ramped with B 101) instead of towards zero; the water level is still relaxed to the still water level. Intended for waves on a current with relaxation wave generation (B 98 2) together with B 60 1 and the discharge W 10: the generation zone then relaxes towards the wave velocity plus U_i, and the inflow ghost cells take over the velocity of the relaxation zone (zero gradient).

B 98.title: Wave Generation Method

options.3: Dirichlet (NHFLOW: with active absorption, see above)
options.4: Dirichlet with Active Absorption, based on shallow water theory (CFD, NHFLOW)

B 98.text: Relaxation generation ramps the solution towards the wave theory inside the generation zone (B 96, B 108) following the relaxation function by ; the zone also absorbs waves reflected back towards the inlet. For the Dirichlet type, waves are generated by assigning the values for the free surface and the velocity at the inflow boundary only, which needs no extra domain length. Active absorption additionally corrects the inflow velocity with the difference between the target and the computed free surface elevation using shallow water theory, U_c = (η_T - η_M)√(g/d), so that reflected waves leave the domain through the inlet. Overrides (control_parse.cpp): B 98 1 (the former two-zone relaxation method by ) is silently changed to B 98 2. For NHFLOW (A 10 5), B 98 3 is changed to B 98 4, i.e.\ Dirichlet generation in NHFLOW always includes active absorption, and B 98 5 is changed to B 98 3 to obtain plain Dirichlet generation without absorption. In SFLOW and FNPF, options 3 and 4 are identical (Dirichlet). In CFD with B 98 2 and W 10 > 0, the discharge of W 10 is imposed at the inlet in addition to the waves. In NHFLOW, the mass-conservative Dirichlet BC A 515 4 imposes the prescribed ma

B 99.title: Numerical Beach Method

options.3: Active Wave Absorption, based on shallow water theory
options.4: Active Wave Absorption, based on intermediate water theory
options.5: Active Wave Absorption, using a flap wavemaker (see B 123)

B 99.text: Both relaxation methods dissipate the wave energy by ramping the free surface down to the still water level, the velocity to zero and the pressure to its hydrostatic distribution for still water conditions inside the beach zone (B 96, B 107). Typically the length of the dissipating relaxation zone should be two wavelengths. Option 1 uses a softer relaxation function than option 2 (the relaxation coordinate is scaled by 1/2). The Active Wave Absorption avoids reflections by generating a wave opposite of the reflected wave at the outflow boundary, thus canceling it out. The method is more efficient in computational terms, as it does not require additional space. Option 4 uses the wave frequency and wave number of the input wave (B 91 or B 93). SFLOW supports options 1–4. In order to use the Active Wave Absorption beach, keep in mind to use the active beach boundary condition in the C data set in DIVEMesh.

B 101.title: Ramp function for wave generation

options.2: ON, t_r = B 102 in s of simulation time

B 101.text: Ramps the generated wave up smoothly from zero, f = t/t_r - (1)/(π)(π t/t_r) for t < t_r, with the ramp duration t_r from B 102.

B 107.title: Numerical beach relaxation zones
B 107.text: The line from (x_start, y_start) to (x_end, y_end) in m defines where the waves are fully damped; the relaxation zone extends the acting distance d in m to both sides of this line, and the damping decreases with the distance from the line. As default, without any user input for B 107, a relaxation zone for the numerical beach is created at the end of the domain, i.e.\ at the maximum x-coordinate of the domain, with an orientation perpendicular to the x-axis over the full domain width, using the distance dist2 from B 96. If user input is provided for B 107, the default relaxation zone will not be created and the input from B 96 will not be used. The B 107 zones are active even without B 99 1 or 2. Multiple numerical beach zones are possible. Beach zones along a domain edge can also be given with B 520 and B 521; they are used in addition to the B 96 or B 107 zones.
B 107.default_text: not set (zone from B 96, see above)

B 108.title: Wave generation relaxation zones
B 108.text: The line from (x_start, y_start) to (x_end, y_end) in m defines where the wave theory is imposed fully; the relaxation zone extends the acting distance d in m to both sides of this line, and the influence of the wave theory decreases with the distance from the line. As default, without any user input for B 108, a relaxation zone for the wave generation is created at the beginning of the domain, i.e.\ at the minimum x-coordinate of the domain, with an orientation perpendicular to the x-axis over the full domain width, using the distance dist1 from B 96. If user input is provided for B 108, the default relaxation zone will not be created and the input from B 96 will not be used. Requires B 98 2. Multiple wave generation zones are possible. Generation zones along a domain edge can also be given with B 520 and B 521; they are used in addition to the B 96 or B 108 zones.

B 111.title: Vertical extent of the flap wavemaker
B 111.text: z-coordinate of the hinge (z_start) and of the top of the flap (z_end) in m for B 92 22 and 24. Must be set when these theories are used.

B 112.title: Vertical extent of the double-hinged flap wavemaker

B 113.title: Second-order wavemaker correction
B 113.text: Second-order wavemaker theory of for the piston, flap and double-hinged flap wavemakers driven by ``wavemaker.dat'' (B 92 21, 22, 23). At start-up the first-order paddle signal is resampled, decomposed by FFT (at most 500 components, frequency band B 114), and the paddle displacement X^(2)(t) that cancels the spurious free second-order waves is added to the input signal. For the double-hinged flap the correction is split over the two flaps in the proportion of the first-order motion. J is the number of evanescent modes per frequency (0: progressive modes only). The water depth is that of the wave theory (B 94). The correction assumes that the paddle reaches above the still water level; a warning is written if B 111 or B 112 z_end lies below it. The applied maximum correction is written to the screen. In FNPF, use together with B 119 1 to include the second-order paddle boundary terms consistently.

B 114.title: Frequency band for the second-order wavemaker correction
B 114.text: Frequencies in Hz for B 113: first-order components between f_min and f_max are used (f_max ≤ 0: chosen automatically; the same band is used for the paddle terms of B 119), and second-order components below f_2,min are not corrected (f_2,min ≤ 0: 0.1 times the peak frequency).

B 115.text: Includes the vertical velocity of the rotating flap (B 92 22, 23) in the generated velocities.

B 116.title: Flap wavemaker kinematics input as paddle motion or angle
B 116.text: Meaning of the second (and third) column in ``wavemaker.dat'' for the flap wavemakers (B 92 22, 23).

B 117.title: Starting time shift for wavemaker kinematics input
B 117.text: Time in s: entries of ``wavemaker.dat'' or ``wavemaker_eta.dat'' before this time are skipped, and the remaining timeseries is shifted to start at t = 0.

B 118.title: Correction factor for the wavemaker velocities
B 118.text: Scaling factor applied to the paddle velocities of the wavemaker theories (B 92 21–24) and to the moving wavemaker objects in the 6DOF module. It was introduced to correct wavemaker generation in NHFLOW.

B 119.title: Moving-paddle boundary condition for FNPF wavemakers
B 119.text: For the piston and flap wavemakers (B 92 21, 22, 23) with Dirichlet generation in FNPF, the inflow velocity φ_x = X_t at x = 0 is extended by the second-order Taylor terms of the moving paddle, X_z φ_z - X φ_xx. These terms are evaluated from the linear paddle solution of the first-order signal (progressive and B 113 J evanescent modes, band B 114), tabulated at start-up, and not from the computed flow. With B 119 1 the numerical paddle behaves like a physical moving paddle, and the B 113 correction then also cancels these terms.

B 260.title: Added mass coefficient c for VRANS porous media
B 260.text: Coefficient of the added mass (inertia) term in the VRANS equations. In NHFLOW all momentum tendencies inside the porous media are scaled with an inertia factor that depends on c and the porosity n (see B 265); in CFD the factor is 1/(1+c) inside the porous media, independent of the porosity. The two modules therefore differ for the same B 260.

B 264.title: number for the VRANS porous media resistance

B 265.title: Inertia factor for NHFLOW VRANS porous media

options.1: n/(1 + c_A) with c_A = c(1-n)/n (VARANS for the superficial velocity, Liu et al.\ 1999)

B 265.text: Selects the inertia (added mass) factor with which all momentum tendencies, including the non-hydrostatic pressure correction, are scaled in NHFLOW where the porosity n < 1, i.e.\ in the VRANS porous media (B 201–B 230) and in the porosity of DEM particles (E 28, see Section ). c is the added mass coefficient B 260. The NHFLOW free surface equation uses the porosity of the surface cell for the storage term. With option 0, long waves in a porous layer travel faster than in open water; option 1 is consistent with this storage term, long waves then travel at √(gh/(1+c_A)). Option 1 is recommended together with the DEM particle porosity (E 28).

B 500.text: Defines a wave train that is superposed (summed) on the B 92 wave in the wave generation and relaxation zones. The B 92 wave is source 1, additional sources need an ID ≥ 2. type is the wave theory as in B 92, H the wave height in m and T the wave period in s (for irregular and focused waves H_s and T_p). The spectrum shape, directional spreading and the water depth are taken from the input of the B 92 wave (B 84–B 88, B 94, B 130–B 136). Wavemaker theories (B 92 20–24), HDC (61) and type 0 are not allowed, and at most one nonlinear wave theory (other than B 92 1, 2, 3, 31, 41, 51) may be used among all sources, including the B 92 wave. Not available with B 89 1. The commands B 500–B 504 must be written as ``B 500 ...'' at the beginning of a line; the equivalent input of all sources is written to the screen at start-up.

B 520.title: Relaxation zone along a domain edge

options.1: wave generation (relaxation towards the wave theory)

B 520.text: Defines a relaxation zone with this ID; its geometry is given with B 521 (required) and its wave sources with B 524. The zones are used in addition to the zones of B 96, B 107 and B 108. A wave generation zone requires B 98 2. A beach zone is active even without B 99 1 or 2 and uses the softer relaxation function of B 99 1 when B 99 1 is selected. Where generation zones overlap, the zone with the highest priority selects the wave sources of the target; the zones of B 96 and B 108 have priority 0, and for equal priority they come first, followed by the B 520 zones in the order given. The adaptive mesh refinement (A 270) does not refine inside B 520 zones. The commands B 520–B 524 must be written as ``B 520 ...'' at the beginning of a line.

D 20.title: Diffusion discretization
D 20.text: Selecting the implicit treatment of the diffusion term in the momentum equations for explicit time stepping has the advantage of removing diffusion from the CFL criterion, which determines the time step size. As the diffusion term enters the CFL criterion in the order of 1/dx^2, effectively larger time steps for D 20 = 2 will be used on especially finer grids. When RANS turbulence models are used, the effective diffusion can be several magnitudes higher than the molecular diffusion. Then implicit diffusion treatment will increase the time step significantly. D 20 also sets the diffusion treatment of the concentration (C 10) and of the turbulence quantities (off for D 20 = 0).

options.2: The wall ghost cells are coupled implicitly to the new velocities: the ghost cell value of the wall boundary condition (B 20, B 23, B 29), written as a linear combination of the two adjacent fluid cells, enters the matrix coefficients. Where this is not possible (e.g. prescribed inflow values), the current ghost cell value is used on the right-hand side.

D 22.text: Treatment of solid neighbour cells in the implicit momentum diffusion (D 20 = 2, not used with VOF-PLIC F 80 = 4). If X 10 > 0 (6DOF), D 22 is set to 2 automatically. With D 22 = 1 and S 10 = 1, the direct-forcing flags are also updated after each bed change.

options.2: second order: implicit-explicit (IMEX) combination, in which the implicit diffusion of each stage is complemented by the explicit diffusion of the earlier stage velocities

options.1: unresolved: particles smaller than the grid
options.2: resolved: particles larger than the grid
options.3: hybrid: per particle, resolved if d_eq/Δ x ≥ E 12, otherwise unresolved

E 11.text: Coupling between the particles and the flow. The equivalent diameter d_eq is that of the sphere with the particle volume; the grid size Δ x is the mean cell size (in NHFLOW the mean horizontal cell size).

E 12.title: Hybrid coupling threshold
E 12.text: With E 11 3, particles with d_eq/Δ x ≥ E 12 are resolved. In NHFLOW, fixed particles larger than E 12 cells give no drag (E 29) and no porosity (E 28 2), only a contact surface.

E 13.title: Maximum number of contact solver iterations
E 13.text: Maximum number of symmetric projected Gauss-Seidel sweeps per DEM step.

E 14.title: Contact solver tolerance
E 14.text: The iterations stop when the largest velocity change of a sweep, relative to max(v_max, 1 mm/s), is smaller than E 14.

E 15.title: print interval
E 15.text: Time interval in s for the VTP files and the state file. With 0, no particle output is written.

E 16.title: Minimum number of DEM substeps
E 16.text: Minimum number of DEM substeps per fluid time step. More substeps are taken automatically when required by E 20 (at most 1000).

E 17.title: Added mass coefficient
E 17.text: Added mass coefficient C_a of unresolved particles.

E 18.title: Resolved coupling: interface half width
E 18.text: Half width of the smoothed Heaviside function of the particle indicator for resolved particles, in cells (at least 0.1).

E 19.title: Penetration correction factor
E 19.text: Fraction of the contact penetration removed per DEM step with split impulses, which move the particles without adding kinetic energy. The correction velocity is limited to 0.5 m/s.

E 20.title: Maximum particle travel per DEM step
E 20.text: Maximum travel of a particle per DEM substep as a fraction of the smallest bounding radius of the moving particles (at least 0.01). The number of substeps per fluid time step is the larger of E 16 and v_maxΔ t/(E 20· r_min).

E 21.title: Contact points per particle pair
E 21.text: Maximum number of contact points kept per particle pair and normal direction cluster (the deepest point and points spread over the contact patch). With 0, all contact points are kept.

E 22.title: Unresolved coupling: fluid acceleration force
E 22.text: Includes the force of the local fluid acceleration (pressure gradient and added mass of the fluid acceleration) on unresolved particles. Floating particles in waves need it to follow the orbital motion.

E 23.title: Unresolved coupling: kernel radius
E 23.text: Radius of the kernel that spreads the reaction force of unresolved particles to the fluid, in cells. The radius is max(d_eq, E 23 Δ x).

E 24.title: Distributed particles: maximum size
E 24.text: With several MPI ranks, particles with a bounding radius up to E 24 times the smallest subdomain extent are distributed: each is owned by the rank that holds its centroid and has copies on the neighbouring ranks. Larger particles are replicated on all ranks; keep their number small. With 0, all particles are replicated. Because contact forces in piles are statically indeterminate, the results depend slightly on the decomposition.

E 25.title: Unresolved coupling: solid volume fraction kernel
E 25.text: Radius of the kernel for the solid volume fraction of unresolved particles, in equivalent diameters. The radius is max(E 25 d_eq, E 23 Δ x). The voidage around a particle (without its own share) enters its drag law.

E 26.title: NHFLOW unresolved coupling: exchange points

options.1: exchange at the volume quadrature points

E 26.text: With 1, the fluid velocity is averaged over the submerged volume quadrature points of each particle (the non-uniform part gives a drag torque), and the reaction is shared by these points and spread from each with a 4-point Peskin kernel. Only with E 11 1 or 3.

E 27.title: NHFLOW unresolved coupling: point-implicit drag
E 27.text: The reaction of the particle drag on the fluid is linearized in the local fluid velocity and applied point-implicitly in every Runge-Kutta stage. This keeps dense beds stable at large time steps. Only with E 11 1 or 3.

E 28.title: NHFLOW: particle volume as porosity

options.2: moving and fixed particles (fixed particles up to E 12 cells)

E 28.text: The submerged volume of the unresolved particles is spread with the momentum kernel and gives the porosity n = 1 - α (n ≥ 0.3), which enters the NHFLOW VRANS terms. With VRANS porous structures (B 200), the two porosities are multiplied. The porosity follows the particles with the relaxation time E 30. Only with E 11 1 or 3. Use it with B 265 1 (Section ); with B 265 0 the VRANS inertia factor makes long waves in the particle layer too fast, and a note is printed.

E 29.title: NHFLOW unresolved coupling: drag of fixed particles
E 29.text: Fixed particles up to E 12 cells exert drag on the fluid, e.g.\ filter layers or fixed toes. Otherwise fixed particles only give a contact surface. Only with E 11 1 or 3.

E 30.title: NHFLOW: relaxation time of the particle porosity
E 30.text: Relaxation time in s with which the porosity of E 28 follows the particles. NHFLOW has no term for the time derivative of the porosity, and an instantaneous porosity (E 30 0) produces spurious flow around moving particles.

F 30.title: Time scheme level set
F 30.text: Activates the level set method for two-phase flow. The level set time scheme is used for the segregated momentum schemes N 40 = 12, 13, 14, 44. For the fully coupled schemes (N 40 = 2, 3, 4, 22, 23, 24, 33) the level set is advanced inside the momentum time scheme, but F 30 > 0 is still required for the two-phase fluid properties.

F 40.title: Reinitialization time scheme
F 40.text: PDE-based reinitialization of the level set function to a signed distance function. F 40 > 0 is also required for the level set initialization with F 51 – F 72 and F 112 – F 115.

F 42.title: Length for initial level set reinitialization
F 42.text: Length in m over which the level set is reinitialized at the start of the simulation; the number of initial reinitialization steps is 2 L/(F 43· dx). If F 42 ≥ 0 it overrides the default length L, which is the maximum domain length. Use it to reduce the initialization time in long domains.

F 43.title: Factor for reinitialization time step size
F 43.text: Pseudo time step of the reinitialization as a fraction of the smallest local cell size: Δτ = F 43· dx. Also used for the PDE-based coastline reinitialization in FNPF (A 339 = 0), for the topography and solid reinitialization (G 40) and for the level set of floating bodies in CFD (X 10).

F 44.title: Number of reinitialization time steps
F 44.text: Number of reinitialization steps per time step (after the initial reinitialization). For the fully coupled momentum schemes (N 40 = 2, 3, 4, 22, 23, 24, 33) and VOF-PLIC (F 80 = 4) this value is set internally for each Runge-Kutta stage.

F 45.title: Factor for the calculation of the interface thickness ε
F 45.text: Half-thickness of the smoothed interface as a multiple of the cell size, ε = F 45· dx, over which density and viscosity change between the phases.

F 46.title: Type of Picard iterations for volume correction

options.2: Volume correction for level set and reinitialization step using the volume from the previous step
options.3: Volume correction for level set and reinitialization step using the total volume balance (inflow and outflow discharge)

F 46.text: Mass conservation correction: the level set is shifted by a constant so that the volume of phase 1 matches the reference volume. The number of iterations is given by F 47.

F 47.title: Number of Picard iterations for volume correction

F 50.title: free surface at inflow or outflow
F 50.text: Selects at which open boundaries the level set function (CFD) or free surface elevation (SFLOW, NHFLOW) is prescribed; at the other open boundaries it is extrapolated.

F 51.title: Phase 1 start, x-direction
F 51.text: Phase 1 (water) is initialized in the box F 51 ≤ x < F 54, F 52 ≤ y < F 55, F 53 ≤ z < F 56. The box is only used if at least one of F 51 – F 56 is given; the large default values mean that the box is not limited in this direction. Setting only F 56 therefore defines a horizontal free surface at z = F 56.

F 57.title: Phase 1 as half-space below a plane
F 57.text: Cells with ax + by + cz < d are set to phase 1. Only active if at least one of the four values is positive.

F 58.title: Phase 1 as sphere
F 58.text: Center coordinates and radius in m of a sphere of phase 1, e.g. a droplet. Only active for r > 0.

F 59.title: Phase 1 as vertical cylinder
F 59.text: Center coordinates, vertical extent and radius in m of a vertical cylinder of phase 1, e.g. a water column. Only active for r > 0.

F 60.title: Initial still water level for the whole domain
F 60.text: Still water level in m (z-coordinate). In CFD it initializes the level set as φ = F 60 - z and overrides F 51 – F 59. In SFLOW, FNPF and NHFLOW it is the reference water level. It is also the starting value of the outflow water level ramp (F 64).

F 61.title: Water level at the inflow boundary
F 61.text: Water level in m (z-coordinate) prescribed at the inflow boundary. In SFLOW it sets the water depth in the inflow ghost cells.

F 62.title: Water level at the outflow boundary
F 62.text: Water level in m (z-coordinate) prescribed at the outflow boundary (use F 50 = 2 or 3). The outflow condition is only applied for F 62 > 0. Use F 64 to ramp up from F 60 to F 62 and F 63 to initialize a sloping free surface.

F 63.title: for linear free surface interpolation
F 63.text: From x = F 63 in m to the end of the domain, the initial free surface is interpolated linearly from the still water level (F 60 or F 56) to the outflow water level F 62. Requires F 62.

F 64.title: Number of iterations for outflow water level ramp up
F 64.text: The outflow water level is ramped from F 60 to F 62 over F 64 time steps with a cosine function. 0 applies F 62 directly.

F 70.title: Phase 1 box
F 70.text: Rectangular box in m that is set to phase 1 (water). Can be used multiple times.

F 71.title: Phase 2 box
F 71.text: Rectangular box in m that is set to phase 2 (air). Can be used multiple times.

F 72.title: Region with prescribed initial water level
F 72.text: In the horizontal region given in m, the initial free surface is set to the water level h in m (z-coordinate). Can be used multiple times, e.g. for dam break cases.

options.4: VOF-PLIC, geometric reconstruction of the interface (under development)

F 80.text: Activates the volume of fluid (VOF) method instead of the level set method; F 35 is then set to 0. The VOF implementation is in beta: the algorithms for open channel flow and wave generation are designed for the level set method. VOF-PLIC (option 4) works with N 40 = 3, 13, 23, 33. The algebraic VOF schemes (former options 1 and 3, with the compression factor F 84) have been removed; REEF3D stops with a message if F 80 = 1 or 3 is given.
