I 12.text: Initializes the pressure field hydrostatically, p = ρ g h, plus the reference pressure I 55. Skipped for options 1–3 if the numerical wave tank is fully initialized (I 30 = 1 together with B 90 > 0). Set automatically to 2 by I 10; reset to 0 if I 40 > 0.

I 13.title: Initialize turbulence model
I 13.text: Calls the initialization of the selected turbulence model (T 10) before the first time step. Set automatically by I 10; reset to 0 if I 40 > 0 or T 10 = 0.

I 21.title: Phase 2 velocities after potential flow initialization
I 21.text: Controls the velocities in the air phase (level set φ < 0) after the potential flow initialization (I 11 > 0).

I 30.title: Full initialization of the numerical wave tank
I 30.text: Initializes the free surface, the velocities (and in FNPF the velocity potential) in the whole domain with the wave theory selected in B 92 at t = 0, instead of only in the wave generation zone. Requires wave generation (B 90 > 0).

I 40.title: Initialization from state file (restart)
I 40.text: Restarts a simulation from a CFD state file written with P 40, selected with I 41. The state files are written per MPI process, so the restart must use the same decomposition (M 10). Simulation time and print counters continue from the state file. Any I 40 > 0 resets I 10–I 13 to 0.

I 41.title: State file number for restart
I 41.text: Number of the state file to restart from (I 40 = 1), i.e.\ the first number in the state file names REEF3D-CFD-State-<number>-<rank>.r3d in the folder REEF3D_CFD_STATE.

I 44.title: Read FNPF state file with 3D velocity potential
I 44.text: When restarting FNPF from a state file, also read the 3D velocity potential (state file written with the potential included, see P 44).

I 50.title: Start time of the simulation
I 50.text: Initial value of the simulation time in s. With a restart (I 40 = 1) the time from the state file is used.

I 55.title: Reference pressure
I 55.text: Constant pressure in Pa used as the initial pressure field and added to the hydrostatic pressure initialization (I 12).

I 56.title: Zero pressure in the air phase
I 56.text: If ON, the hydrostatic pressure of the pressure initialization (I 12) is set to zero above the free surface (level set φ < 0).

I 58.title: Initial vertical velocity around the F 58 sphere
I 58.text: Sets the vertical velocity to w_0 in m/s inside the sphere defined by F 58 and decreases it linearly to zero between the F 58 radius and the radius r_2 in m (r_2 larger than the F 58 radius). Active for r_2 > 0, e.g.\ for droplet impact cases.

I 230.title: Read FlowFile for inflow boundary condition
I 230.text: Uses a FlowFile (velocities, pressure, level set over time) from a previous 2D CFD simulation, printed with P 230, as inflow boundary condition. The number is the ID of the FlowFile gage. When active, the iowave wave generation at the inflow (B 98) is bypassed, so B 98 should be set to 0. See also I 231.

I 231.title: x-offset for hydrodynamic coupling input; vertical offset of FlowFile inflow
I 231.text: For hydrodynamic coupling (B 92 = 61), shift in m added to the x-coordinate when the input data is interpolated to the current grid. For FlowFile inflow (I 230, CFD), vertical offset in m of the FlowFile profile, rounded to whole cells.

I 232.title: y-offset for hydrodynamic coupling input
I 232.text: For hydrodynamic coupling (B 92 = 61), shift in m added to the y-coordinate when the input data is interpolated to the current grid.

I 233.title: z-offset for hydrodynamic coupling input
I 233.text: For hydrodynamic coupling (B 92 = 61), shift in m added to the z-coordinate (relative to the still water depth) when 3D input data (from FNPF or NHFLOW) is interpolated to the current grid.

I 240.text: Not in the user guide yet.

I 241.title: Time offset for hydrodynamic coupling input and FlowFile inflow
I 241.text: For hydrodynamic coupling (B 92 = 61), time in s added to the current wave time when the input data is read and interpolated in time, i.e.\ the coupling starts at time I 241 of the source simulation. For FlowFile inflow (I 230, CFD), time in s added to the simulation time when the FlowFile is interpolated in time.

L 10.title: Lagrangian particle tracking
L 10.text: Activates the particle tracking for NHFLOW (A 10 5). The particles are defined with L 21 – L 23. The NHFLOW mesh refinement (A 270) does not support particles and is switched off when L 10 1 is set.

L 11.title: Random seed
L 11.text: Seed of the random numbers for the random walk (L 31, L 32). Each process uses the seed plus a process-dependent offset. Change the seed to obtain an independent realization of the random walk.

L 21.title: Point release
L 21.text: Releases n particles at the point (x, y, z) in m. The release times are distributed evenly over [t_s, t_e) in s; with t_e ≤ t_s all particles are released at t_s. w_s is the rise velocity in m/s (w_s > 0: buoyant, w_s < 0: settling), c_w the windage coefficient as fraction of U_10 (e.g.\ 0.01 – 0.05 for floating plastics with emerged area). With mode 0 the particles move in three dimensions, with mode 1 they are trapped at the free surface and z is ignored. z is given in the absolute vertical coordinate of the grid (the same as for the probes, P 65); a particle released above the free surface is placed on it, one released below the bed is reflected into the water column (or deposited, L 52). x and y are given in world coordinates.

L 22.title: Line release
L 22.text: Releases n particles along the line from (x_s, y_s, z_s) to (x_e, y_e, z_e) in m, evenly spaced at the positions s = (q+0.5)/n, q = 0 … n-1, along the line. For a release over a time window, the particles are released in this order, i.e.\ the line is seeded from start to end over the window. The remaining values are the same as for L 21.

L 23.title: Box release
L 23.text: Releases n particles at uniformly distributed random positions inside the box in m. The positions are reproducible and do not depend on L 11 or on the domain decomposition. The remaining values are the same as for L 21.

L 31.title: Horizontal diffusivity K_h
L 31.text: Constant horizontal diffusivity in m^2/s for the random walk. It represents the dispersion by processes that are not resolved by the grid. It does not act on stranded or deposited particles.

L 32.title: Vertical diffusion
L 32.text: Vertical random walk of the three-dimensional particles (mode 0). With option 2 the diffusivity is K_v(z) = K_v,0 + ν_t/Sc_t with the background value L 33, the eddy viscosity ν_t of the NHFLOW turbulence model (A 560) and the turbulent Schmidt number L 34; the gradient of K_v is taken into account with the drift correction of .

L 33.title: Vertical diffusivity K_v,0
L 33.text: Constant (L 32 1) or background (L 32 2) vertical diffusivity in m^2/s.

L 41.title: Wind for windage
L 41.text: Wind speed at 10 m height (m/s) and the direction it blows towards (deg), measured counter-clockwise from the positive x-axis, as for A 571. The windage c_w U_10 of each release acts on the particles at the free surface. If L 41 is not given and the NHFLOW wind forcing is active (A 570 > 0), the values of A 571 are used. Note that the wind stress of A 570 – A 578 already drives a surface current in NHFLOW; c_w should therefore only represent the direct wind drag on the emerged part of the particles.

L 51.title: Beaching

options.0: stranded, refloat at the free surface when the cell becomes wet again

L 51.text: Treatment of stranded particles, i.e.\ particles in dry cells (wetting and drying, A 540 – A 544). Stranded particles are placed on the bed and do not move.

L 52.title: contact

options.1: deposition of settling particles (w_s < 0), reflection of all others

L 52.text: Treatment of three-dimensional particles that reach the bed. Deposited particles stay on the bed; resuspension is not included.

L 53.title: Lateral domain boundaries
L 53.text: Treatment of particles that leave the horizontal extent of the computational domain. The boundary type from DIVEMesh is not taken into account. Removed particles are counted in the log file.

L 61.title: Print interval
L 61.text: Output interval of the particle files in s of simulated time. With a value ≤ 0 the particles are written every time step. The first output is written at the start of the simulation.

L 62.title: Output format

options.3: VTP files and CSV track file

L 62.text: The log file is always written.

M 10.title: Number of processes for parallel computations
M 10.text: Must be set, also for serial runs (M 10 1). The value must equal the M 10 used in DIVEMesh to decompose the grid and the number of MPI processes REEF3D is started with (e.g.\ mpirun -n 4 for M 10 4). REEF3D compares all three at start-up and stops with the message ``Inconsistent M 10 parameter'' if they differ.

N 10.title: Linear solver for the Poisson/Laplace equation

options.1: REEFMG, BiCGStab with semicoarsening multigrid (SFLOW, FNPF, NHFLOW, CFD)

N 10.text: Selects the solver for the Laplace equation of the velocity potential (FNPF), the pressure equation (NHFLOW, CFD, non-hydrostatic SFLOW) and the potential flow initialization (I 11). The default is REEFMG (N 10 1), REEF3D's own multigrid solver, which is available in every build and in all four modules. The HYPRE solvers (N 10 11–38) are only available if REEF3D is compiled with HYPRE support (make HYPRE=1); HYPRE is optional and not part of the default build. In a build without HYPRE, any N 10 ≥ 10 is replaced by N 10 1 at start-up and a message is printed, so input files written for the HYPRE solvers run with REEFMG. With HYPRE, use a matching preconditioner in N 11. The fastest HYPRE combination is the Struct BiCGStab solver with PFMG preconditioning (N 10 14, N 11 11); from the HYPRE AIJ solvers, PCG with BoomerAMG (N 10 21, N 11 21) is fastest. For more information on the HYPRE solvers and preconditioners, see the HYPRE user manual . Module restrictions: SFLOW accepts 1 and 11–19 (HYPRE Struct 2D); without HYPRE it always uses REEFMG. The internal BiCGStab solver (3) with Jacobi preconditioning works for the CFD pressure only. HYPRE AIJ (21–25) and SStruct (31–38) work for FNP

N 11.title: Preconditioner for the Poisson/Laplace equation
N 11.text: Preconditioner for the HYPRE Krylov solvers selected in N 10, i.e.\ only used in builds with HYPRE (make HYPRE=1); use only options from the same solver family. The multigrid solvers used on their own (N 10 18, 19, 25, 38), REEFMG (N 10 1) and the internal BiCGStab (N 10 3) ignore N 11. With HYPRE Struct and PFMG (11), N 20 together with N 23, N 25 or N 26 can switch the preconditioner to SMG during the run.

N 12.title: REEFMG line smoother

options.0: one forward sweep before and one backward sweep after the coarse-grid correction
options.2: red-black line smoother (experimental, slower on CPUs)

N 12.text: Ordering of the vertical line relaxation in REEFMG (N 10 1).

N 13.title: REEFMG maximum number of coarse levels
N 13.text: Limits the number of coarsening steps per horizontal direction in REEFMG (N 10 1). With 0 the grid is coarsened until a local extent falls below 8 cells.

N 14.title: REEFMG multigrid precision
N 14.text: Floating-point precision of the REEFMG multigrid hierarchy (N 10 1). With 32 the hierarchy is stored in single precision (about 25% less solver memory and a faster V-cycle); the BiCGStab iteration and the convergence test remain in double precision, so the converged result is unchanged. Any other value uses double precision.

N 15.title: REEFMG coarse-grid agglomeration
N 15.text: If ON, the coarsest REEFMG level (N 10 1) is gathered onto every rank and solved there, which replaces many halo exchanges by one all-gather per V-cycle and may pay off at high numbers of processes. It is refused if the gathered problem is too large.

N 18.title: Index ordering of the HYPRE Struct grid
N 18.text: Ordering of the grid axes passed to HYPRE Struct (N 10 11–19, builds with HYPRE only). Option 2 makes the vertical index the fastest-running one; it is implemented for the FNPF Laplace equation and the NHFLOW pressure only.

N 20.title: Iteration threshold for preconditioner switch
N 20.text: Only in builds with HYPRE: if a HYPRE Struct solve with PFMG preconditioning (N 11 11) needs more than N 20 iterations, the preconditioner is switched to SMG for the rest of the simulation. The switch is enabled per module with N 23 (FNPF), N 25 (NHFLOW) and N 26 (CFD).

N 22.text: Not in the user guide yet.

N 23.title: Preconditioner switch for FNPF
N 23.text: Enables the PFMG-to-SMG preconditioner switch (N 20) for FNPF.

N 24.text: Not in the user guide yet.

N 25.title: Preconditioner switch for NHFLOW
N 25.text: Enables the PFMG-to-SMG preconditioner switch (N 20) for NHFLOW.

N 26.title: Preconditioner switch for CFD
N 26.text: Enables the PFMG-to-SMG preconditioner switch (N 20) for CFD.

N 40.title: Time scheme for the momentum equations

options.14: 3rd-order low-storage Runge-Kutta (separate free surface), with its own time loop; direct-forcing variant for 6DOF (X 10 = 1) or FSI (Z 10 > 0). With DEM fluid coupling (E 10 > 0, E 11 > 0), the DEM forcing of the fluid is not applied with this option (a warning is printed).
options.33: 3rd-order TVD Runge-Kutta (momentum-free surface coupled), conservative formulation with face densities

N 40.text: In the coupled schemes the free surface (level set or VOF) is advanced within the Runge-Kutta stages of the momentum equations; in the separate schemes the level set is advanced with its own time scheme (F 30 = 2 or 3). Options 22, 23 and 24 are identical to 2, 3 and 4. With PLIC (F 80 = 4), options 3, 23, 13 and 33 use their PLIC variants. Override: with 6DOF (X 10 > 0), N 40 = 3 or 23 is changed to 4 and N 40 = 13 to 14. The former option 5 (3rd-order Runge-Kutta with Crank-Nicolson diffusion) has been removed; selecting it stops the simulation with a message.

N 41.title: Maximum simulated time
N 41.text: End time of the simulation in s. Of N 41 and N 45, whichever criterion is reached first ends the simulation.

N 43.title: Stopping criterion for the convection-diffusion solver
N 43.text: Convergence tolerance of the iterative solver for the implicit transport equations (implicit diffusion, turbulence, scalars), i.e.\ the internal BiCGStab solver and the HYPRE Struct/SStruct BiCGStab used for these equations.

N 44.title: Stopping criterion for the Poisson/Laplace solver
N 44.text: Convergence tolerance of the solver selected in N 10 (pressure, Laplace and potential flow equations) and of the SFLOW solvers.

N 45.title: Maximum number of time steps
N 45.text: Maximum number of outer iterations (time steps). Of N 41 and N 45, whichever criterion is reached first ends the simulation.

N 46.title: Maximum number of solver iterations
N 46.text: Maximum number of iterations of the linear solvers per solve. REEFMG prints a warning when the limit is reached. The SFLOW potential flow initialization and the CFD potential flow initialization in the water phase (I 11 2) use a fixed limit of 2500.

N 47.title: Relaxation factor for time step size
N 47.text: Safety factor (Courant number) that multiplies the maximum stable time step from the CFL criterion for adaptive time stepping (N 48 1). In SFLOW with the Boussinesq option A 220 = 4 values above 0.25 are reduced to 0.25.

options.1: ON, time step from the CFL criterion with N 47

N 49.title: Time step size for fixed time stepping
N 49.text: Time step in s for fixed time stepping (N 48 0). In FNPF and NHFLOW it is also the upper limit of the adaptive time step.

N 50.title: Adaptive time stepping method

options.1: standard, based on the velocity magnitude and the smallest cell size
options.2: component-wise, based on each velocity component and the cell size in that direction (less conservative)

N 50.text: Formulation of the CFL criterion for adaptive time stepping in CFD (N 48 1).

N 60.text: Not in the user guide yet.

N 61.title: Critical velocity for emergency stop
N 61.text: If the maximum velocity in any direction exceeds this value in m/s, the simulation stops and writes a final output file. In FNPF, velocities in the first five cells at x_min are additionally limited to 0.95 · N 61.

P 10.title: Format of the 3D field output (ParaView binary)
P 10.text: The 3D files are written into REEF3D_<M>_VTU, REEF3D_<M>_VTS or REEF3D_<M>_VTR for FNPF, NHFLOW and CFD. VTR is only available for CFD; in FNPF and NHFLOW option 3 switches the 3D output off. SFLOW writes 2D VTP files instead (REEF3D_SFLOW_VTP_FSF and REEF3D_SFLOW_VTP_BED, see P 181), which are only written for P 10 = 1.

P 11.text: Not in the user guide yet.

P 12.title: Terminal and log print frequency
P 12.text: Writes the iteration summary to the terminal and to the log files in REEF3D_Log (main, max, solver and volume log) every n^th iteration. Use larger values to reduce terminal output for long simulations.

P 15.title: Numbering of the output files
P 15.text: Applies to the 3D and VTP field files and to most other numbered output files.

P 16.title: time stamp to ParaView files
P 16.text: Writes the simulation time as TimeValue field data into the VTU/VTS/VTR and VTP files, so that ParaView shows the physical time instead of the file number. For the 3D files the sediment time is used when P 34 > 0.

P 18.text: Not in the user guide yet.

P 19.title: Print interval for NHFLOW and FNPF floating body files

options.2: VTP interval: P 181, P 182 or P 185

P 19.text: Selects which print-out interval is used for the floating body VTP/STL files in REEF3D_<M>_6DOF_VTP and REEF3D_<M>_6DOF_STL. In CFD the floating body files always follow the 3D interval (P 20, P 30, P 35), in SFLOW always the VTP interval (P 181, P 182, P 185).

P 20.title: Print 3D results every n^th iteration
P 20.text: Writes the 3D field files (see P 10) into REEF3D_<M>_VTU. Only active if P 30 and P 34 are negative. Choose one of P 20, P 30, P 34 or P 35. For SFLOW use P 181. Also sets the interval of the floating body files in CFD (and NHFLOW and FNPF with P 19 = 1). With adaptive mesh refinement in FNPF and NHFLOW (A 270 > 0), the refined patches are written with the same interval as VTR files with a .vtm multiblock index into REEF3D_<M>_AMR, in addition to the regular 3D files.

P 21.title: Print time-averaged velocity, pressure and temperature
P 21.text: Adds velocity_mean, pressure_mean and, with heat transfer (H 10), T_mean to the CFD VTU files. Averaging starts at the time given with P 22.

P 22.title: Start time for time averaging
P 22.text: Simulation time in s after which the averaging for P 21 starts. Set it after the initial transients have left the domain.

P 23.title: Print test array
P 23.text: Adds the internal test array to the 3D files and the VTP files. Used for debugging and development.

P 24.title: Print density to the VTU file
P 24.text: Adds the density rho in kg/m^3. Ignored for multiphase flow (F 300 > 0), which writes its own density field.

P 25.title: Print solid to the VTU file
P 25.text: Adds the solid level set function solid. In NHFLOW, the Heaviside function of the solid is written as well.

P 26.title: Print suspended sediment concentration to the VTU file
P 26.text: Adds ST_conc. Use together with sediment transport (S 10).

P 27.title: Print topo to the VTU file
P 27.text: Adds the bed level set function topo. Set to 1 automatically when sediment transport is active (S 10 ≥ 1) or when a topography is read from the DIVEMesh grid file.

P 28.title: Print floating body level set function
P 28.text: Adds the floating body level set function (floating in the 3D files, fb in the SFLOW and NHFLOW free surface VTP files).

P 29.title: Print wall distance to the VTU file
P 29.text: Adds walldist, the distance to the nearest wall in m.

P 30.title: Print 3D results every t seconds
P 30.text: Time-based alternative to P 20, writes into REEF3D_<M>_VTU. Only active if P 34 is negative. Choose one of P 20, P 30, P 34 or P 35. For SFLOW use P 182. Also used for the AMR output of FNPF and NHFLOW (see P 20).

P 34.title: Print 3D results every t seconds of sediment time
P 34.text: Uses the morphological (sediment) time instead of the hydrodynamic time. Only active if P 30 is negative. Choose one of P 20, P 30, P 34 or P 35.

P 35.title: Print 3D results in a time window
P 35.text: Writes the 3D files every Δ t seconds between t_start and t_end (all in s). Several windows can be defined; they act in addition to P 20 or P 30. In CFD the floating body files follow these windows as well.

P 37.text: Not in the user guide yet.

P 38.text: Not in the user guide yet.

P 39.text: Not in the user guide yet.

P 40.title: Print state files
P 40.text: Writes binary state files into REEF3D_<M>_STATE with the interval of P 41 or P 42. They are used for restart (see I 40 for full initialization from a state file), for hydrodynamic coupling (HDC, e.g.\ SFLOW or FNPF to CFD; see the H options in the DIVEMesh manual for building the HDC input from state files) and for grid nesting. The CFD state file contains the velocities, pressure, level set function, k, eddy viscosity, ε or ω, topo, cbed and conc. With the particle sediment model (Q 10 ≥ 1), the particles are written into additional files REEF3D-CFD-CPM-State-<n>-<rank>.r3d in the same folder. Related commands: P 43 to P 47.

P 41.title: Print state files every n^th iteration
P 41.text: Only used if P 42 is negative. With the default, a state file is written every iteration when P 40 = 1.

P 42.title: Print state files every t seconds
P 42.text: Time-based alternative to P 41. For hydrodynamic coupling, match the interval to the time step expected by the receiving simulation (see I 241).

P 43.title: Print area for state files
P 43.text: Restricts the state files of P 40 to the given horizontal area in m. Reduces the file size when only a part of the domain is needed, e.g.\ for HDC or nesting. Without P 43 the whole domain is written.

P 44.title: Components of the FNPF and NHFLOW state files

options.1: η, free surface potential, velocities (standard for HDC)
options.2: η, free surface potential, velocities, 3D potential
options.3: η, free surface potential (more efficient for FNPF nesting)

P 44.text: For FNPF the options below apply. For NHFLOW, η and the velocities are always written; P 44 = 1 adds the pressure.

options.1: single file per print-out (numbered according to P 15)

P 46.title: Iteration window for state files
P 46.text: State files (P 40, P 41) are only written for iterations i_start ≤ n < i_end.

P 47.title: Time window for state files
P 47.text: Intended to restrict the time-based state files (P 40, P 42) to t_start ≤ t < t_end. Note: the code currently reads both values as integers and compares them with the iteration number, not the simulation time.

P 50.title: Wave gauge for the theoretical wave
P 50.text: Location in m. Records the free surface elevation of the wave theory selected for wave generation every time step into REEF3D_<M>_WSF/REEF3D-<M>-WSF-HG-THEORY.dat. Requires wave generation (B 90). Useful for comparing with P 51 at the same locations.

P 51.title: Wave gauge
P 51.text: Location in m. Records the simulated free surface elevation every time step into REEF3D_<M>_WSF/REEF3D-<M>-WSF-HG.dat, one column per gauge. In CFD the surface is found from the level set function (from the VOF function for F 80 = 4). With adaptive mesh refinement (A 270 > 0) in SFLOW, FNPF and NHFLOW, the elevation at the same gauges is additionally taken from the finest grid level holding each gauge and written into REEF3D_<M>_AMR/REEF3D_<M>_AMR_gauges.dat.

P 52.title: Free surface line in x-direction
P 52.text: y-location in m of a line along the x-direction. The free surface along the line is written into REEF3D_<M>_WSFLINE, one file per print-out with the interval of P 54 or P 55.

P 53.title: the theoretical wave to the free surface line files
P 53.text: Adds the free surface of the wave theory to the files of P 52 and P 56. Requires wave generation (B 90).

P 54.title: Print line output every n^th iteration
P 54.text: Interval for the free surface lines (P 52, P 56), the CFD line probes (P 62), the SFLOW depth-averaged probes (P 63) and the NHFLOW profiles and line probes (P 67, P 144). Only used if P 55 is negative (P 63 always uses P 54).

P 55.title: Print line output every t seconds
P 55.text: Time-based alternative to P 54 for P 52, P 56, P 62, P 67 and P 144.

P 56.title: Free surface line in y-direction
P 56.text: x-location in m of a line along the y-direction. Written into REEF3D_<M>_WSFLINE_Y with the interval of P 54 or P 55.

P 57.title: Additional output for the FNPF wave gauges
P 57.text: Intended to add the rise velocity ∂η/∂ t and the horizontal free surface velocity at the P 51 gauges, in REEF3D_FNPF_WSF/REEF3D-FNPF-Rise-Velocity.dat and REEF3D_FNPF_WSF/REEF3D-FNPF-Horiontal-FSF-Velocity.dat. Note: this output is currently not functional in the code. The value after P 57 is not read; the option is set by the number of P 57 lines in ctrl.txt, and only the file headers are written.

P 58.title: Theoretical wave time series
P 58.text: Writes the free surface elevation of the wave theory at (x,y) in m from t=0 to T in s, sampled every 0.1 s, into REEF3D_Log-Wave/REEF3D-Wave-Timeseries-<n>.dat. The series is computed once at the start of the simulation. Requires wave generation (B 90); not written for B 92 = 20, 21, 22, 23 and 61. If no P 58 is given, one series at (0,0) with T = 12800 s is written.

P 59.title: Print breaking wave log
P 59.text: Writes the time and the (x,y) location of every cell flagged as breaking, every time step, into REEF3D_FNPF_Breaking_Log.

P 61.title: Point probe
P 61.text: Location in m. Records u, v, w, p, k, ε or ω and the eddy viscosity every time step into REEF3D_CFD_ProbePoint/REEF3D-CFD-Probe-Point-<n>.dat.

P 62.title: Line probe
P 62.text: Start and end point of the line in m. Writes x, y, z, u, v, w, p, k, ω, eddy viscosity and level set function along the line into REEF3D_CFD_ProbeLine, one file per print-out with the interval of P 54 or P 55.
P 62.default_text: na ; na ; na ; na ; na ; na

P 63.title: Depth-averaged point probe
P 63.text: Location in m. Records the depth-averaged velocities U, V, W, the pressure, η and the bed level every P 54 iterations into REEF3D_SFLOW_ProbePoint/REEF3D-SFLOW-Probe-Point-<n>.dat.

P 64.title: Pressure probe
P 64.text: Location in m. Records the pressure every time step into REEF3D_CFD_PressureProbe/REEF3D-CFD-Probe-Pressure-<n>.dat (CFD) or REEF3D_NHFLOW_ProbePoint/REEF3D-NHFLOW-Probe_Press-<n>.dat (NHFLOW).

P 65.title: Velocity probe
P 65.text: Location in m. Records u, v, w (FNPF also the potential) every time step into REEF3D_<M>_ProbePoint/REEF3D-<M>-Vel-Probe-<n>.dat.

P 66.title: Velocity probe for the theoretical wave
P 66.text: Location in m. Records the velocities of the wave theory every time step into REEF3D_<M>_ProbePoint/REEF3D-<M>-Vel-Probe-Theory-<n>.dat. Requires wave generation (B 90).

P 67.title: Vertical velocity profile
P 67.text: Location in m. Writes the vertical profile of the horizontal velocity u over z into REEF3D_NHFLOW_U-Profile/REEF3D-NHFLOW-U-Profile-<n>-<i>.dat (with i the iteration number), one file per print-out with the interval of P 54 or P 55.

P 68.text: Not in the user guide yet.

P 69.text: Not in the user guide yet.

P 71.title: Print viscosity to the VTU file
P 71.text: Adds the molecular viscosity field in m^2/s.

P 72.title: Print VOF function to the VTU file

Q 10.title: Sediment model type
Q 10.text: Requires S 10 1 or 2. Options 1 and 2 select the particle model and the time scheme of the MP-PIC sub-steps (Q 11 2); the plain model Q 11 1 always uses a two-stage Runge-Kutta scheme. With the hydrostatic pressure scheme D 30 10 the fluid density is blended to the sediment density S 22 below the bed level.

options.1: plain particle transport: drag against the frictional resistance Q 30, two-stage Runge-Kutta time stepping with the sediment time step S 13 – S 15
options.2: MP-PIC: drag (Q 51), fluid pressure gradient, gravity and inter-particle stress (Q 12), adaptive sub-steps within the flow time step, time scheme Q 10

Q 12.title: Inter-particle stress model

options.1: Snider (2001): τ = P_s θ^β/(θ_cs-θ,\ ε(1-θ)) with the parameters Q 14 – Q 17
options.2: packed bed: effective stress of the contact network plus contact pressure (Q 32 – Q 35) and Coulomb friction (Q 13, Q 36 – Q 38). The submerged weight (ρ_s-ρ_w)|g|θ of the bed (θ ≥ Q26 (1-n)) is integrated downwards from the top of the bed, which carries the grains of a bed at rest without compaction. The contact pressure P_c = F_r(θ-θ_0)^η_0/(θ_max-θ)^η_1 of Johnson and Jackson (1987) acts against compaction beyond θ_0 = 1-n; it is continued linearly above θ_0 + 0.5(θ_max-θ_0).

Q 12.text: Normal stress τ of the particle phase for Q 11 2; it acts on the parcels with -τ/(θρ_s).

Q 13.title: Frictional stress for the packed bed model
Q 13.text: Coulomb friction of each parcel on the bed below it (Q 12 2), treated implicitly. The normal load follows from the support by the contact network. The slip relative to the bed is stopped below the static friction coefficient μ_s (Q 36), otherwise it is reduced with μ(I) = μ_s + (μ_2-μ_s)/(I_0/I+1) of the μ(I) rheology, with the inertial number I = d_50γ/√(P/ρ_s) (Q 37, Q 38). A slope fails at β = μ_s.

Q 14.title: Pressure constant P_s of the Snider stress model

Q 15.title: Exponent β of the Snider stress model

Q 16.title: Parameter ε of the Snider stress model
Q 16.text: Small number that bounds the denominator of the stress near close packing. Used with Q 12 1.

Q 17.title: Critical solid volume fraction θ_cs of the Snider stress model
Q 17.text: Close packing solid volume fraction at which the stress rises steeply. Used with Q 12 1.

Q 18.title: Courant number for the particle stress wave speed
Q 18.text: The MP-PIC sub-step (Q 11 2) is limited to Δ t_sub ≤ Q18 · h_min/c, where c = √((dτ/dθ)/ρ_s) is the wave speed of the inter-particle stress and h_min the smallest cell size. In addition the particle Courant number S 14 limits the sub-step with the maximum parcel velocity.

Q 19.title: Grid-limited step
Q 19.text: Packing limit as kinematic constraint on the grid for Q 11 2: in each sub-step a parcel enters a new cell only if that cell has free volume, with the capacity (θ_max V,\ (1-n)V + V_parcel) (Q 32). The requests for a cell are served in the order of their arrival time; a rejected parcel stops at the cell face and its velocity into the full cell is removed. Cells inside solid bodies have no free volume.

Q 24.title: Number of particles per cell

If Q 24 is not set, one parcel per cell is used and a warning is printed.

Q 25.title: Safety factor for the parcel allocation
Q 25.text: Initial size of the parcel arrays relative to the number of seeded parcels. Values below 1.0 are set to 1.0.

Q 26.title: Solid fraction threshold of the bed interface
Q 26.text: The bed surface is the iso-surface θ = Q26 (1-n) of the solid volume fraction, with the porosity n (S 24). With Q 12 2 the same threshold separates the bed, which carries the contact network stress and the friction, from suspended sediment.

Q 27.title: Number of smoothing passes for the solid volume fraction
Q 27.text: Passes of a conservative explicit filter (zero flux at walls) applied to the solid volume fraction θ after the parcel volumes are distributed to the grid.

Q 29.text: Parcels above the bed or inside solid bodies are removed after seeding.

Q 30.title: Friction factor for the particle resistance force
Q 30.text: Dimensionless friction coefficient of the resistance force F_s = Q30 (ρ_s-ρ_w) |g| π d_50^3/6 of a grain. The driving drag force is reduced by F_s and set to zero where it is smaller than F_s. Used with Q 11 1.

Q 32.title: Maximum solid volume fraction θ_max
Q 32.text: Close packing limit. It is the singularity of the contact pressure (Q 12 2), the cell capacity of the grid-limited step (Q 19) and sets the minimum fluid fraction 1-θ_max in the drag law, the two-way coupling and the VRANS porosity. Values ≤ 0 give θ_max = 1-n+0.035 with the porosity n (S 24); θ_max > 1-n is required.

Q 33.title: Contact pressure coefficient F_r
Q 33.text: Coefficient in Pa of the contact pressure of Johnson and Jackson (1987) for Q 12 2; 0 switches the contact pressure off.

Q 34.title: Contact pressure exponent η_0
Q 34.text: Exponent of (θ-θ_0) in the contact pressure for Q 12 2.

Q 35.title: Contact pressure exponent η_1

Q 36.title: Static friction coefficient μ_s
Q 36.text: Friction coefficient of the packed bed (Q 12 2, Q 13 1); it sets the angle of repose μ_s and the threshold of motion of an exposed grain.

Q 37.title: Dynamic friction coefficient μ_2
Q 37.text: Limit of the friction coefficient μ(I) for large inertial numbers (Q 12 2, Q 13 1).

Q 38.title: Inertial number scale I_0
Q 38.text: Scale of the inertial number in the μ(I) friction law (Q 12 2, Q 13 1).

Q 50.title: Fluid coupling of the parcels

options.0: one-way: the fluid sees the bed as solid boundary (S 10 1) or as VRANS porous region with the porosity 1-θ (S 10 2)

Q 50.text: Two-way coupling requires Q 11 2. The reaction of the parcel drag is added to the fluid momentum equations as a point-implicit source term, the drag uses the interstitial fluid velocity u/(1-θ), and the mixture continuity ·u = -·(θu_p) enters the pressure Poisson equation. With S 10 2 the bed is then neither a solid boundary nor a VRANS region for the fluid; the fluid flows through the parcels and feels their drag.

S 10.title: Sediment transport module

options.1: ON, impermeable sediment bed (SFLOW, NHFLOW, CFD)
options.2: ON, porous sediment bed with VRANS (CFD only, requires A 10 6; porosity S 24, VRANS coefficients S 26)
options.12: ON, fully coupled RK2 sediment time stepping (NHFLOW only)

S 10.text: Switches on morphodynamics. Any value >0 also activates the topography handling (G 1 is set to 1) and the printing of the bed (P 27 is set to 1). In REEF3D::CFD the particle-based sediment model is selected with Q 10 1 or 2 instead of the default Exner-based model (see section Q).

S 11.title: Bedload transport formula

options.3: Engelund and Freds e (dynamic friction coefficient S 18)

S 11.text: Equilibrium bedload transport capacity q_b,e used in the Exner equation. All formulas use d_50 (S 20), the sediment density (S 22) and the critical Shields parameter (S 30).

S 12.title: Suspended sediment transport
S 12.text: Solves an implicit advection-diffusion equation for the suspended sediment concentration with the settling velocity from S 23/S 25. The near-bed reference concentration follows van Rijn; its reference height is set with S 61, the coupling with the Exner equation with S 62.

S 13.title: Maximum sediment time step
S 13.text: Upper limit of the morphodynamic time step in s for S 15 0, and the fixed time step for S 15 2.

S 14.title: Courant number for the sediment time step
S 14.text: The morphodynamic time step is decoupled from the hydrodynamic time step (see S 15). It is determined from a Courant criterion on the rate of bed elevation change, Δ t_sed = S14 · Δ x / |∂ z_b/∂ t|. For the plain particle model (Q 11 1) the maximum parcel velocity is used instead of the bed change rate; for the MP-PIC particle model (Q 11 2) S 14 limits the parcel sub-steps within the flow time step, Δ t_sub ≤ S14 · h_min/|u_p| (see Q 18). Recommended range: 0.1 – 0.5.

S 15.title: Sediment time step selection

options.0: adaptive: minimum of S 13 and the Courant criterion S 14
options.1: adaptive: minimum of the flow time step and the Courant criterion S 14
options.3: flow solver time step (Exner model only)

S 15.text: All options are multiplied by the factor S 17 (Exner model only). The MP-PIC particle model (Q 11 2) always uses the flow time step with adaptive sub-steps; options 0 – 2 apply to the plain particle model (Q 11 1).

S 16.title: shear stress formulation

options.1: wall function / log-law, velocity based (SFLOW: Manning formulation with k_s)
options.2: log-law, velocity based, limited from below by the turbulent kinetic energy (SFLOW: depth-averaged log-law)
options.3: viscosity based: τ = ρ(ν+ν_t) u/Δ z (SFLOW: depth-averaged log-law)
options.4: turbulent kinetic energy based: τ = 0.3 ρ k
options.5: geometric mean of options 1 and 4 (CFD only)
options.6: depth-averaged velocity, Chezy (CFD) or Manning (NHFLOW) formula
options.7: log-law with the grain roughness, horizontal velocity only (CFD only)
options.8: log-law with iterative roughness correction for transitional flow (CFD only)

S 16.text: The available options depend on the flow model. Log-law based options use the effective roughness k_s = S21 · d_50 (see also S 36).

S 17.title: Factor for the sediment time step
S 17.text: Dimensionless factor applied to the sediment time step selected with S 15 (for S 15 1 and 3 it multiplies the flow time step). Values >1 accelerate the morphodynamics relative to the hydrodynamics (morphological acceleration). Not used by the particle model and not applied when S 29 is used.

S 18.title: Dynamic friction coefficient μ_d for the Engelund and Freds e bedload formula

S 19.title: Maximum simulated sediment time
S 19.text: The simulation stops when the accumulated morphodynamic time reaches S 19 in s (in addition to the limits N 41 and N 45). The default is a large sentinel value, i.e.\ inactive.

S 20.title: Sediment grain size d_50
S 20.text: Median grain diameter in m. It enters the transport formulas, the critical bed shear stress, the bed roughness (S 21) and, for the particle model, the parcel size.

S 21.title: Roughness factor
S 21.text: The equivalent sand roughness of the sediment bed is k_s = S21 · d_50. It is used in the bed shear stress calculation (S 16), with S 28 1 in the wall boundary condition of the flow over the bed and, for the MP-PIC particle model with S 10 1, in the logarithmic law for the fluid velocity at the parcels near the bed surface.

S 23.title: Sediment settling velocity
S 23.text: Settling velocity w_s in m/s used for suspended sediment transport. Only used if the automatic calculation is switched off (S 25 0).

S 24.title: Porosity of the sediment bed
S 24.text: Volume fraction of pores n in the bed. It enters the Exner equation as 1/(1-n), the VRANS porosity for S 10 2, and the parcel size and packing limit of the particle model.

S 25.title: Automatic settling velocity calculation
S 25.text: When ON, w_s is calculated from d_50, the sediment and water densities and the viscosity W 2: Stokes law for d_50<0.1 mm, the van Rijn formula for 0.1 ≤ d_50 < 1 mm and 1.1g d_50(ρ_s/ρ_w-1) for d_50 ≥ 1 mm.

S 26.title: VRANS resistance coefficients for the porous sediment bed
S 26.text: Dimensionless linear (α) and non-linear (β) resistance coefficients of the VRANS porous media model inside the sediment bed. Only used with S 10 2 and A 10 6.

S 27.title: Number of Exner sub-iterations per sediment step
S 27.text: Number of times the Exner equation (and the sandslide algorithm) is advanced with Δ t_sed during one call of the sediment module, without updating the bed shear stress and transport rates in between.

S 28.title: Roughness of the sediment bed in the flow boundary condition
S 28.text: Selects the roughness used in the wall boundary condition of the hydrodynamics (velocities and turbulence) at the sediment bed when S 10 >0.

S 29.title: Sediment time step ramp
S 29.text: Linear ramp of the maximum sediment time step from Δ t_s to Δ t_e (in s) between the sediment times t_s and t_e (in s). Before t_s the value Δ t_s, after t_e the value Δ t_e is used. The ramped value limits the Courant-based time step (S 14); S 15 and S 17 are then ignored. Exner model only.

S 30.title: Critical Shields parameter
S 30.text: θ_cr for incipient motion on a flat bed. The critical bed shear stress is τ_cr = r θ_cr (ρ_s-ρ_w) g d_50 with the slope reduction factor r (S 80).

S 31.title: Type of Exner formulation

options.1: scalar q_b, upwinding with the flow direction at the cell faces
options.2: vector flux (q_b s_x, q_b s_y) with the cell-centred flow direction
options.3: directional derivative of q_b along the cell-centred flow direction

S 31.text: Determines how the transport direction enters the divergence of the bedload flux.

S 33.title: Non-equilibrium bedload transport

options.1: constant adaptation length L_s = S 40 in m
options.2: van Rijn (1984) saltation length L_s = 3 d_50 D_*^0.6 T^0.9

S 33.text: With non-equilibrium transport the bedload flux q_b relaxes towards the transport capacity q_b,e over the adaptation length L_s along the transport path, q_b + L_s s· q_b = q_b,e. The equation is solved with a Gauss-Seidel method in every sediment step (maximum number of sweeps S 49). For options 2 and 3, L_s is typically only a few grain diameters, so the result is practically identical to equilibrium transport on usual grids.

S 34.title: Type of suspended load bed change calculation
S 34.text: Currently without effect: the implicit suspended sediment solver used for S 12 1 does not evaluate this option.

S 35.title: Exner magnification factor
S 35.text: Dimensionless factor multiplying the bed change rate in the Exner equation (morphological acceleration). It is also included in the bed celerity limit S 103.

options.0: grain roughness only, k_s = S21 · d_50
options.1: grain roughness plus van Rijn's bedform roughness, based on the transport stage and the water depth

S 37.title: Inertia contribution to the bed shear stress
S 37.text: Adds a bed shear stress contribution from the horizontal flow acceleration, τ_acc = ρ_w c_m c_v c_n S21 d_50 |∂ u/∂ t|, to the effective bed shear stress (NHFLOW only).

S 38.title: Blend bed shear stress with shallow water formulation
S 38.text: In very shallow water the bed shear stress is blended with a depth-averaged Manning-type formulation (NHFLOW only). The blending starts below the water depth h = S39 · A544; below 0.5 S39 · A544 only the shallow water formulation is used.

S 39.title: Blending depth factor for S 38
S 39.text: Dimensionless factor on the wetting and drying threshold A 544 that sets the water depth where the shallow water blending of S 38 starts. With the defaults this is 100 · 0.001 m = 0.1 m.

S 40.title: Adaptation length for non-equilibrium bedload transport
S 40.text: Adaptation length L_s in m for S 33 1, or dimensionless factor on the water depth for S 33 4.

S 41.title: Type of sediment start criterion

options.3: flow simulation time divided by the wave period, t/T (S 47)

S 41.text: Sediment transport starts once the criterion is reached; before that only the bed shear stress is calculated.

S 42.title: Type of sediment interval criterion
S 42.text: Interval between two calls of the sediment module (Exner model only; the particle model is called every flow time step).

S 43.title: Number of flow iterations before sediment transport starts
S 43.text: Used with S 41 1. Also the start of the erosion-deposition coupling of suspended sediments (S 62 1) and of the NHFLOW RK2 sediment model (S 10 12).

S 44.title: Number of flow iterations between bed updates

S 45.title: Flow simulation time before sediment transport starts

S 46.title: Flow simulation time between bed updates

S 47.title: before sediment transport starts
S 47.text: Number of wave periods before sediment transport starts; used with S 41 3. Requires a wave generation with a defined wave period.

S 48.title: between bed updates
S 48.text: Number of wave periods between two bed updates; used with S 42 3.

S 49.title: Maximum number of Gauss-Seidel sweeps for non-equilibrium bedload
S 49.text: Upper limit of sweeps per sediment step for S 33 >0; the iteration stops earlier at convergence (relative tolerance 10^-6).

S 50.title: Fixed bed level at inflow or outflow boundary
S 50.text: Boundary condition for the bed level at the inflow and outflow boundaries: a fixed bed does not change there, otherwise the bed level is extrapolated.

S 51.title: Sediment fraction for a graded bed
S 51.text: Each S 51 line defines one grain size class of a multi-fraction (graded) sediment bed: the diameter d_k in m, its initial volume fraction in the active layer F_a,k and in the substrate F_s,k. Between 1 and 20 fractions are allowed; without S 51 the bed has a single fraction with d_50 = S 20. The fractions of each layer are normalized to a sum of 1; if all F_s,k are zero, the substrate gets the composition of the active layer. The bed consists of an active (mixing) layer of thickness S 52 on top of one well-mixed substrate layer of thickness S 53 (Hirano active-layer model). The bedload formula S 11 is evaluated once per fraction with d_k, i.e.\ with the Shields parameter θ_k = τ_b/((ρ_s-ρ) g d_k) and the critical Shields parameter S 30 (including the slope reduction S 80) multiplied by the hiding/exposure factor (S 54), and the capacity is weighted with the local fraction in the active layer. The Exner equation, the sandslide and the bed relaxation zones act on each fraction, so that the volume of each fraction is conserved. Not available with the RK2 sediment solver S 10 12. The fractions and the local d_50, d_m, d_90 and substrate thickness are added to the sediment output (ST_Fk

S 52.title: Active layer thickness
S 52.text: Thickness L_a in m of the active layer of the graded bed (S 51). With a value ≤ 0, L_a = 2 d_90 of the initial active-layer composition.

S 53.title: Initial substrate layer thickness
S 53.text: Initial thickness in m of the substrate layer below the active layer of the graded bed (S 51). The substrate grows with deposition and shrinks with erosion.

S 54.title: Hiding/exposure function
S 54.text: Correction of the critical Shields parameter of each fraction of the graded bed (S 51) for hiding of fine grains between coarse grains and exposure of coarse grains. With option 1, θ_cr,k is multiplied by ξ_k = (p_e,k/p_h,k)^-m with p_h,k = _j F_j d_j/(d_k+d_j), p_e,k = 1 - p_h,k and the exponent m from S 55 .

S 55.title: Hiding/exposure exponent m
S 55.text: Exponent of the hiding/exposure function S 54 1.

S 56.title: Grain size for the bed roughness of a graded bed
S 56.text: Diameter d in the bed roughness k_s = S 21 · d when a graded bed (S 51) is used. Options 1–3 use the local grain size of the active layer, so that the roughness follows the bed sorting.

S 57.title: Initial flat sediment bed level
S 57.text: Sets a horizontal sediment bed at the elevation z = S 57 in m over the whole domain, overriding the topography from the grid. The default sentinel value means not set.

S 60.text: Not in the user guide yet.

S 61.title: Near-bed concentration for suspended sediment

options.1: concentration of the first cell above the bed
options.2: first cell concentration extrapolated to the reference height 2 d_50 with the Rouse profile

S 61.text: Concentration c_b at the reference level used for the erosion-deposition balance with S 12 1.

S 62.title: Coupling of suspended sediment with the Exner equation

options.1: erosion-deposition term w_s (c_b - c_b,e) is added to the Exner equation (after S 43 iterations)
options.2: depth-integrated suspended load flux is added to the bedload flux (computed by NHFLOW)

S 66.text: Not in the user guide yet.

S 71.title: Start of the erodible region in x-direction
S 71.text: The Exner equation is only solved for S71 ≤ x ≤ S72, and the slope reduction of the critical shear stress (S 80) is only applied there. The default sentinel means no limit. For smooth transitions S 73 or S 75 are preferred.

S 72.title: of the erodible region in x-direction

S 73.title: Relaxation zone for the sediment bed along a line
S 73.text: Inhibits sediment transport near a straight line through (x_0, y_0) in m and makes it smoothly transition to the active bed over the given distance in m. On the line the bed is held at the elevation z_b in m and the bed change, transport rates and bed shear stress are set to zero; they are blended with a smooth function to their computed values at the given distance. The line angle β is given in degrees; β = 0 gives a line parallel to the y-axis, i.e.\ the distance is measured in x-direction. Several lines can be combined.

S 74.title: Non-erodible rectangular zone
S 74.text: The bedload transport is set to zero inside the rectangle x_s < x < x_e, y_s < y < y_e (in m). Several zones can be defined.

S 75.title: Relaxation zone for the sediment bed in x-direction
S 75.text: Within the given distance in m from x = x_0 in m, the bed is smoothly relaxed towards its initial level and the transport rates and bed shear stress are reduced, reaching zero at x_0. This method is preferred over S 71 and S 72 because of the smooth transition of the sediment bed. Several locations can be defined.

S 77.title: Active region of the bed update algorithms in x-direction
S 77.text: Restricts the bed filter (S 100), the sandslide algorithm (S 90), the relaxation S 73 and the transfer of the bed level to the CFD topography to x_s < x < x_e (in m).

S 78.title: Inflow guard
S 78.text: When ON, the bed is kept fixed in the cells at the inflow boundary and at inflow patches of the patchBC (B 400s).

S 79.text: Not in the user guide yet.

S 80.title: Critical shear stress reduction for a sloping bed

options.5: Fredse, with longitudinal and transverse parts weighted by the flow direction

S 80.text: Reduces or increases the critical bed shear stress on sloping beds with the factor r, limited to 0.01 ≤ r ≤ 1.5. Uses the angle of repose S 81/S 82.

S 81.title: Angle of repose
S 81.text: Mean angle of repose φ in degrees. The effective angle varies between φ ± S 82 depending on the direction of the bed slope relative to the flow. Used by S 80 and the sandslide algorithm S 90.

S 82.title: Variation of the angle of repose Δφ

S 83.text: Not in the user guide yet.

S 84.title: Limiter for the critical bed shear stress reduction

options.1: Fredse: reduction factor clipped to 0.01 ≤ r ≤ 1.5
options.2: function based: r = 0.1/|γ| + 0.1 for slopes above the angle of repose

S 84.text: Treatment of the reduction factor of S 80 where the bed is steeper than the angle of repose.

S 85.title: Bedload direction correction
S 85.text: Corrects the bedload direction for the bed slope using the method proposed by Koch and Flokstra (1980).

S 90.title: Sandslide algorithm
S 90.text: Corrects bed slopes that exceed the angle of repose (S 81, S 82) after each bed update. Iterations S 91, correction factor S 92, extra angle S 93, calling interval S 94.

S 91.title: Maximum number of sandslide iterations
S 91.text: The iteration stops earlier when no cell needs correction.

S 92.title: Sandslide correction factor
S 92.text: Dimensionless factor on the bed level correction per sandslide iteration (S 90 1 – 4).

S 93.title: Delta angle for the sandslide correction
S 93.text: Additional angle in degrees by which an over-steep slope is flattened below the angle of repose (S 90 1 and 2).

S 94.title: Sandslide interval
S 94.text: The sandslide algorithm is called every S 94 sediment iterations.

S 100.title: Number of outer bed filter iterations
S 100.text: Spatial smoothing of the bed change rate before the bed update, restricted to sediment cells within S 77. Larger numbers increase the filter effect; 0 switches the filter off. The filter weight is S 102.

S 101.title: Number of inner bed filter iterations
S 101.text: Corrector iterations of each outer filter iteration (Van Cittert sharpening). Larger numbers move the bed change closer to the unfiltered values; recommended range 1 – 5.

S 102.title: filter weight
S 102.text: Weight of the centre cell in the bed filter, f = S102 h + (1-S102) h_neighbours. A value of 1.0 means no smoothing, smaller values smooth more.

S 103.title: celerity Courant number for the sediment time step
S 103.text: Additionally limits the sediment time step with the celerity of bed forms, Δ t_sed ≤ S103 Δ x/c with c = S35/(1-n) ∂ q_b/∂ z_b. Only bed level differences larger than d_50 are considered. 0.0 switches the limit off.

T 10.title: Turbulence model
T 10.text: Turbulence model of REEF3D::CFD. The turbulence models of SFLOW and NHFLOW are selected with A 260 and A 560. The EARSM option T 10 12 has been removed; the run stops with a message, use T 10 2 instead.

T 12.title: Convection discretization for the turbulence model

T 23.title: coefficient for the URANS filter
T 23.text: Dimensionless coefficient of the URANS eddy viscosity filter of the k-ω model (T 10 22).

T 31.title: Factor for the eddy viscosity limiter
T 31.text: Coefficient of the strain-based limiter ν_t ≤ T31 · k/|S| (activated with T 34 in CFD, A 564 in NHFLOW).

T 33.title: Turbulent kinetic energy source term in the momentum equations
T 33.text: Adds the isotropic part of the Reynolds stresses, -(2)/(3) k, as source term to the momentum equations (two-equation models).

T 34.title: Eddy viscosity limiter
T 34.text: Strain-based eddy viscosity limiter of the k-ω model, with the coefficient T 31.

T 36.title: Free surface boundary condition for the turbulent dissipation

options.2: ON, including the distance from the nearest wall
options.3: ON, including the water depth (k-ω only)

T 36.text: Sets the specific dissipation near the free surface to damp the turbulence there, using the virtual origin T 37 and the interface width T 38.

T 37.title: Virtual origin for the distance y' above the free surface
T 37.text: Used by the free surface dissipation boundary condition (T 36 in CFD, A 567 in NHFLOW); for T 36 3 or A 567 3 it is a dimensionless factor on the water depth.

T 38.title: Width factor for the free surface turbulence damping
T 38.text: Half-width ε of the free surface zone for T 36 and T 39, as a multiple of the average cell size.

T 39.title: Minimum eddy viscosity at the free surface
T 39.text: Within the free surface zone (width T 38) the eddy viscosity of the k-ω model is limited from below by a Smagorinsky subgrid-scale eddy viscosity (C_s = 0.2).

T 41.title: k-ω stabilization
T 41.text: Stabilization of the eddy viscosity in nearly potential flow regions after Larsen and Fuhrman (2018), with the coefficient T 42. For NHFLOW use A 565.

T 42.title: Coefficient λ_2 for the k-ω stabilization
T 42.text: Coefficient of the stabilization limiter (T 41 in CFD, A 565 in NHFLOW); smaller values give a weaker limitation.

T 43.text: Not in the user guide yet.

T 44.title: Height factor for the wall velocity at the sediment bed
T 44.text: In the k-ω wall boundary condition at a sediment bed (S 10 >0) the velocity is interpolated at the height T 44 · Δ z above the bed.

T 45.title: Buoyancy term in the k-equation
T 45.text: Adds turbulence production or damping due to density stratification (k-ω model).

W 3.title: Density of phase 2 (air)
W 3.text: In FNPF and NHFLOW only used for the wind forcing and, in NHFLOW, for the parts of nets above the free surface.

W 5.title: Surface tension coefficient
W 5.text: Surface tension between phase 1 and phase 2; 0.0 switches surface tension off.

W 6.title: Density of phase 3
W 6.text: Density of the third fluid (e.g.\ oil) for the multiphase level set model (F 300).

W 7.title: Kinematic viscosity of phase 3
W 7.text: Viscosity of the third fluid for the multiphase level set model (F 300).

W 10.title: Discharge
W 10.text: Inflow discharge used by ioFlow (B 60) and by the wave generation with current.

W 11.title: Inflow velocities on surface 1
W 11.text: Fixed velocities in m/s on surface 1 (requires an inflow boundary condition on surface 1 in DIVEMesh). Options W 11 – W 16 are made for benchmark and other simple test and validation cases. For more complex and real world cases, either B 60 1 (ioFlow) or the B 400s (patchBC) options are recommended.

W 12.title: Inflow velocities on surface 2
W 12.text: Requires an inflow boundary condition on surface 2 in DIVEMesh; see W 11.

W 13.title: Inflow velocities on surface 3
W 13.text: Requires an inflow boundary condition on surface 3 in DIVEMesh; see W 11.

W 14.title: Inflow velocities on surface 4
W 14.text: Requires an inflow boundary condition on surface 4 in DIVEMesh; see W 11.

W 15.title: Inflow velocities on surface 5
W 15.text: Requires an inflow boundary condition on surface 5 in DIVEMesh; see W 11.

W 16.title: Inflow velocities on surface 6
W 16.text: Requires an inflow boundary condition on surface 6 in DIVEMesh; see W 11.

W 20.title: Acceleration due to gravity, x-component
W 20.text: In FNPF only used in the force calculation of floating bodies, in NHFLOW in the force calculation of floating bodies, for DEM particles (E 10) and for the rod trees (Z 20); SFLOW only uses W 22.

W 22.title: Acceleration due to gravity, z-component
W 22.text: Must be set for all free surface simulations, typically -9.81.

W 29.title: Additional constant pressure gradient
W 29.text: Constant source term added to the momentum equations like a body force, i.e.\ the pressure gradient divided by the density in m/s^2, e.g.\ to drive the flow with periodic boundary conditions.

W 30.title: Compressibility of air
W 30.text: Calculates the density of phase 2 from the ideal gas law using the local pressure and the temperature W 31.

W 41.title: Velocity vertical line source for phase 1
W 41.text: Vertical line source at (x_c, y_c) in m between z_s and z_e in m with the velocity U in m/s. Here, β is the direction of the flow in degrees.

W 50.title: inflow velocity
W 50.text: Velocity in m/s in x-direction imposed in the air phase at the inflow boundary, e.g.\ to model wind. Only active if the command is given.

W 90.title: Non-Newtonian rheology

options.1: Herschel-Bulkley (yield stress W 96 or W 101, consistency W 97, exponent W 98)
options.2: three-phase mixture: Herschel-Bulkley slurry (W 98, W 105, W 106) and Coulomb viscoplastic gravel (W 106, W 107), weighted with W 108 (CFD only)

W 90.text: Rheology of phase 1. In SFLOW only option 1 is available, as a Bingham-type bed friction.

W 95.title: Maximum kinematic viscosity ν_0
W 95.text: Upper limit of the rheological viscosity for W 90 >0; it regularizes the viscosity at vanishing shear rates.

W 96.title: Yield stress τ_0
W 96.text: Prescribed yield stress for W 101 0. It is also used in the first time step for all W 101 options.

W 97.title: Consistency index K
W 97.text: Consistency index of the Herschel-Bulkley model, τ = τ_0 + K γ^n, in Pa s^n.

W 98.title: Power law index n
W 98.text: n<1: shear thinning, n>1: shear thickening, n=1: Bingham fluid.

W 101.title: Yield stress model

options.2: Drucker-Prager type, τ_0 = (p φ + c)(1-e^-W103 γ)
options.4: as 3, with shear rate generated excess pore pressure, p e^-W104 γ
options.5: as 3, with linear shear rate coupling, p - W104 γ

W 101.text: Pressure-dependent yield stress models use the angle of repose and cohesion W 102, the pressure selected with W 111 and the regularization W 103. Options 3 – 5 use the buoyant part of the pressure (interstitial fluid density 1000 kg/m^3). SFLOW supports options 0 and 1.

W 102.title: Angle of repose and cohesion for the Mohr-Coulomb yield stress
W 102.text: Angle of repose φ in degrees and cohesion c in Pa, used with W 101 >0.

W 103.title: Transition factor for the Mohr-Coulomb yield stress
W 103.text: Regularization time scale in s in the factor (1-e^-W103 γ) of W 101 2 – 5; larger values give a sharper transition.

W 104.title: Shear rate coupling factor for the pore pressure
W 104.text: Coefficient of the shear rate dependent reduction of the effective pressure: time scale in s for W 101 4, and coefficient in Pa s for W 101 5.

W 105.title: Slurry yield stress parameters for W 90 2
W 105.text: Calibration yield stress τ_00 in Pa (accounts for the grid dependency of the shear rate), total volumetric solid concentration C, and the volumetric concentrations of kaolinite and chlorite C_kc, illite C_i and montmorillonite C_m (all in m^3/m^3). The slurry yield stress is τ_y = τ_0 C^2 e^22 C P_1, with τ_0 = τ_00 for C<0.47 and τ_0 = τ_00 e^5(C-0.47) otherwise, and P_1 derived from C_kc + 1.3 C_i + 1.7 C_m.

W 106.title: Slurry consistency factor and gravel regularization for W 90 2
W 106.text: The slurry consistency is k = b τ_y. m_y in s is the regularization parameter of the Coulomb viscoplastic gravel viscosity, μ = μ_min + p δ (1-e^-m_yγ)/γ.

W 107.title: Gravel viscosity parameters for W 90 2
W 107.text: Minimum dynamic viscosity μ_min in Pa s, internal friction angle δ in degrees and maximum dynamic viscosity μ_max in Pa s of the Coulomb viscoplastic gravel phase. Note that the default μ_max = 0 switches the gravel viscosity off, so it must be set.

W 108.title: Slurry volume fraction a_2 for W 90 2
W 108.text: The mixture viscosity is (a_2 μ_slurry + (1-a_2)μ_gravel)/ρ, with ρ = W 1 as mean density of the mixture.

W 110.title: Numerical treatment of the rheology

options.1: viscosity for rheology and yield stress
options.2: viscosity for rheology, momentum source term for yield stress
options.3: momentum source term for rheology and yield stress
options.4: viscosity for rheology, yield stress gradient as momentum source term
options.5: rheology and yield stress gradient as momentum source term
options.6: viscosity for rheology, frictional source term from the pressure gradient, φ p

W 110.text: Determines whether the viscous (rheology) part and the yield stress part of the Herschel-Bulkley model enter as viscosity or as momentum source term.

W 111.title: Pressure for the Mohr-Coulomb yield stress

options.3: hydrostatic pressure away from the interface and total pressure close to the interface (see W 112)
options.4: average of hydrostatic and total pressure
options.5: hydrostatic for the first 10 iterations, total pressure afterwards

W 112.title: Threshold factor for W 111 3
W 112.text: The total pressure is used where the level set distance from the interface is smaller than W 112 · Δ x.

X 10.title: Turn on 6DOF algorithm for floating bodies

options.1: Two-way coupling: body motion from the hydrodynamic forces (CFD, NHFLOW and FNPF)
options.2: One-way coupling: the body moves according to X 11 and the prescribed or initial velocities without hydrodynamic feedback (SFLOW and NHFLOW)
options.3: Ship-wave mode: the body acts as an external moving pressure field on the free surface (SFLOW and NHFLOW, requires X 400)
options.4: Prescribed wavemaker geometry from X 170 or X 172 driven by wavemaker.dat (NHFLOW)

X 10.text: Activates the rigid-body module. In FNPF (A 10 3) the bodies are resolved in the Laplace problem (Section ); moorings and the power take-off (X 500) are supported there, nets are ignored. Whenever X 10 > 0, D 22 is set to 2, and the NHFLOW/CFD time scheme N 40 is changed from 3 or 23 to 4 and from 13 to 14.

X 11.title: Degrees of freedom of the floating body
X 11.text: Sets the treatment of the three linear (u, v, w) and three angular (p, q, r) velocities individually. Prescribed degrees of freedom take their velocity from X 210/X 211 or from a motion file (X 240). In 2D simulations the sway velocity v and the rotations p and r are always switched off; fixed and prescribed degrees of freedom receive no hydrodynamic load and no damping (X 25, X 26).

X 12.text: Not in the user guide yet.

X 14.title: Preserve tangential velocities for forcing
X 14.text: Controls how the body velocity is imposed by the direct forcing in CFD. With 1, cells inside the body receive the full rigid-body velocity, while in the smoothing layer outside the body (X 41) each velocity component is forced only with the weight of the corresponding component of the surface normal, which preserves tangential velocities.

X 15.title: Type of direct forcing near the body surface for NHFLOW

options.0: full forcing of all velocity components (no-slip)
options.1: full forcing inside the body; outside, each component weighted with the magnitude of the corresponding normal component
options.2: full forcing inside the body; outside, only the normal velocity component is forced (free slip, tangential velocity preserved)

X 15.text: Controls how the body velocity is imposed by the direct forcing in NHFLOW (also for the X 10 4 wavemakers). The forcing layer thickness is set with A 526.

X 16.title: Porous floating body
X 16.text: Treats the NHFLOW floating body (X 10 1) as a moving porous medium instead of a rigid body imposed by direct forcing. Given are the porosity n of the body, the characteristic grain or element size d_50 in m and the linear (Darcy) and quadratic (Forchheimer) resistance coefficients α and β, with the same closure as the NHFLOW VRANS objects (B 201; the KC correction B 264 is applied as well). The porosity field 1 - H(1-n) follows the body, and the Darcy-Forchheimer resistance acts on the fluid velocity relative to the body velocity; it is integrated implicitly over each Runge-Kutta stage, so that large coefficients remain stable. Its reaction is added to the body forces (written to the viscous force columns of the force file), the pressure load on the body surface is scaled with (1-n), and no viscous wall forces are computed on the envelope. The forces are always integrated over the triangulated surface (as X 60 1). Can be combined with static VRANS structures (B 200 1). Giving X 16 activates the porous body.

X 17.text: Not in the user guide yet.

X 18.text: Not in the user guide yet.

X 19.title: Print out interval for 6DOF log files
X 19.text: The 6DOF log files (position, velocity and forces in the folder REEF3D_*_6DOF) are written every X 19 time steps. Also used for the FSI log files (Z 10).

X 20.title: Number of floating bodies
X 20.text: Number of 6DOF bodies in CFD. Body 0 reads its geometry from floating.stl, body n ≥ 1 from floating-n.stl (X 180 1). All other X settings are shared by all bodies. NHFLOW and SFLOW always use one body.

X 21.title: Floating body homogeneous density ρ in [kg/m^3]
X 21.text: The mass is computed from this density and the body volume. The density is used by default; if X 22 is given, X 22 takes precedence. For a porous floating body (X 16), X 21 and X 22 define the mass of the solid skeleton, i.e.\ X 21 is the bulk density ρ_s(1-n).

X 22.title: Floating body mass m in [kg]
X 22.text: If given, the mass is prescribed and the density is computed from mass and body volume; X 21 is then ignored.

X 23.title: Floating body centre of gravity in [m]
X 23.text: If not given, it is calculated from the geometry. The centre of gravity is also the origin of the body-fixed (non-inertial) coordinate system and the centre of rotation.

X 24.title: Floating body moments of inertia in [kg m^2]
X 24.text: Principal moments of inertia about the centre of gravity. If given, the products of inertia are set to zero. If not given, the full inertia tensor is calculated from the geometry and the density.

X 25.title: Damping coefficients for rotational motion around the three axes
X 25.text: Linear damping moment -C ω added to the moment balance of the solved rotational degrees of freedom, in [N m s].

X 26.title: Damping coefficients for translational motion along the three axes
X 26.text: Linear damping force -C u added to the force balance of the solved translational degrees of freedom, in [N s/m].

X 38.title: Type of viscous force calculation on the body surface

options.0: CFD: viscous stresses from the local velocity gradients with the molecular viscosity; NHFLOW: no viscous force
options.1: CFD: wall-gradient approximation with molecular and eddy viscosity; NHFLOW: skin friction with C_f = 10^-4
options.2: CFD: logarithmic wall function (roughness k_s = 10^-5 m)

X 38.text: Used with the STL force calculation (X 60 1). The velocity is sampled at the distance X 43 from the surface.

X 41.title: Thickness of the continuous direct forcing layer
X 41.text: Half-width of the smoothed Heaviside function around the body surface, in multiples of the mean cell size. In CFD it is used for floating bodies and for the direct forcing of solids and topography. In SFLOW and in the NHFLOW ship-wave mode (X 10 3) it sets the width of the pressure field transition; otherwise NHFLOW uses A 526.

X 42.title: Distance for pressure force evaluation
X 42.text: Distance from the surface triangles along the outward normal at which the pressure is interpolated for the force integration (X 60 1), in multiples of the local cell size.

X 43.title: Distance for shear stress evaluation
X 43.text: Distance from the surface triangles along the outward normal at which the velocities are interpolated for the viscous forces (X 38), in multiples of the local cell size.

X 45.title: Type of free surface level set convection discretization at the floating body

options.0: standard stencil, convection also inside the floating body
options.1: gradients set to zero for stencil cells closer than 0.6 dx to the body surface
options.2: gradients weighted with the averaged body indicator function
options.3: gradients set to zero inside the body
options.4: gradients weighted with the upwind body indicator function
options.5: gradients set to zero inside solids and topography
options.6: gradients inside the body set to a large value (10^20)

X 45.text: Modifies the stencil of the fifth-order WENO Hamilton-Jacobi scheme near the floating body. Only effective with F 35 5.

X 48.title: Level set extrapolation into direct forcing solids
X 48.text: If ON, the level set and the k-ω turbulence quantities are copied from the first fluid cell into the two adjacent cells inside direct-forcing bodies (floating bodies, solids, topography).

X 50.title: Type of print out format for 6DOF structure
X 50.text: Since the VTP print out is binary, it is significantly faster than the STL print out. This becomes runtime relevant for STL files with a large number of triangles.

X 60.title: Type of hydrodynamic force calculation
X 60.text: With 1 the pressure (X 42) and viscous stresses (X 38, X 43) are integrated over the surface triangles. With 2 the forces are computed from a triangulation reconstructed from the level set function; the surface refinement X 185 is then skipped.

X 101.text: Rotates the body around its centre of gravity at the start. Positive angles rotate the body clockwise. Mooring end points on the body are rotated with it only if X 313 1.

X 102.title: Initial linear floating body velocity in [m/s]
X 102.text: If given several times, the values are added.

X 131.text: Radius r, length h and centre point (x_c, y_c, z_c) in [m]. The cylinder is triangulated with circumferential segments of about 0.75 dx (at least 8).

X 132.title: Cylinder in y-direction floating body
X 132.text: Radius r, length h and centre point (x_c, y_c, z_c) in [m]. Triangulated as X 131.

X 133.title: Cylinder in z-direction floating body
X 133.text: Radius r, height h and centre point (x_c, y_c, z_c) in [m]. Triangulated as X 131.

X 163.text: Each of the 6 corner points is given by its coordinates in [m], see the figure below.

X 164.text: Each of the 8 corner points is given by its coordinates in [m], see the figure below.

X 170.title: Piston wavemaker in [m]
X 170.text: Box-shaped piston moved with the displacement time series in wavemaker.dat (columns t [s], x [m]; time shifted by X 241). Requires X 10 4.

X 171.title: Flap wavemaker in [m]
X 171.text: Intended for X 10 4; currently not implemented.

X 172.title: Double-hinged flap wavemaker in [m]
X 172.text: Requires X 10 4. The motion is read from wavemaker.dat (columns t [s], horizontal displacement of the lower and of the upper flap segment [m], or angles in [rad] with B 116 2); lines with t smaller than B 117 are skipped.

X 180.title: Read STL file floating.stl for floating body geometry
X 180.text: The file must be in ASCII STL format. With X 20 > 1, the further bodies are read from floating-1.stl, floating-2.stl, …

X 181.title: Scale STL geometry in x-, y-, and z-direction
X 181.text: Scaling factors applied to the STL coordinates, before X 182 and X 183.

X 182.title: 3D linear translation of STL object in [m]
X 182.text: Applied after the scaling X 181 and before the rotation X 183.

X 183.title: 3D rotation of STL object
X 183.text: Rotation around the point (x_origin, y_origin, z_origin) in [m] by the angles in [deg], applied after X 181 and X 182. Positive angles rotate the body clockwise.

X 184.title: Hole filling for the surface remeshing

options.0: OFF, holes are kept as open boundaries
options.1: close gaps and fill holes with a harmonic (flat, membrane-like) patch
options.2: close gaps and fill holes with a biharmonic (curvature-continuous) patch

X 184.text: Treatment of open boundaries of the body surface with X 185 4. Gaps between nearly coincident edges are closed and holes are patched; if the surface was repaired, the volume and the mass (X 21) or density (X 22) are computed from the closed surface. With 0, a warning is printed if the surface is not closed.

X 185.title: Type of geometry refinement for triangulated surface mesh

options.2: split, based on global minimum dx
options.3: split, based on local minimum dx
options.4: remeshing to the local grid spacing

X 185.text: Options 1 – 3 split surface triangles whose mean edge length exceeds the critical length (reference cell size times X 186) into four. Option 4 re-triangulates the whole surface with an adaptive isotropic remesher: the target edge length is X 186 times the local cell size of the fluid grid (X 190), sharp edges (X 187), corners and open boundaries are preserved, all vertices stay on the original surface and holes are closed (X 184). The remeshing is done on one process and broadcast, so the result does not depend on the domain decomposition. If the estimated number of triangles exceeds 2·10^6, the input triangles are kept (increase X 186). For sigma grids (NHFLOW, FNPF), the vertical cell size is taken from the still water column, and with mesh refinement around the body the horizontal cell size is that of the finest refinement level. The refinement is skipped for X 60 2 and for the wavemakers X 170–X 172.

X 186.title: Geometry refinement factor for triangulated surface mesh
X 186.text: Critical triangle size for X 185 1 – 3, or target edge length for X 185 4, relative to the reference cell size, i.e.\ in numbers of fluid cells.

X 187.title: Feature angle for the surface remeshing
X 187.text: Edges between surface triangles whose normals differ by more than this angle in degrees are treated as sharp features and preserved by the remeshing (X 185 4).

X 188.title: casting algorithm for the floating body level set

options.1: directional ray casting in x-, y- and z-direction

X 188.text: Method used to compute the distance function of the body from the surface triangles in CFD.

X 189.title: Number of iterations for the surface remeshing
X 189.text: Number of split, collapse, flip and relaxation cycles of the remeshing (X 185 4).

X 190.title: Cell size for the surface remeshing

options.1: grid metric: the target length is set per direction, so that every edge spans about X 186 cells in each direction (triangles stretched like the cells)
options.2: geometric mean of the cell spacings dx, dy, dz (isotropic)

X 190.text: Local cell size that is multiplied with X 186 to give the target edge length of the remeshing (X 185 4). Only the active grid directions are used (no y in 2D, no z for a single cell layer).

X 205.title: Ramp up function type
X 205.text: Shape of the ramp functions X 206 and X 207.

X 206.title: External motion ramp up start time and end time in [s]
X 206.text: Ramps the prescribed velocities (X 210, X 211, X 240) from zero at t_s to full value at t_e; before t_s the prescribed velocities are zero.

X 207.title: Draft ramp up start time and end time in [s]
X 207.text: Ramps the external pressure field of the ship-wave mode (X 10 3, X 400). Without X 207 the free surface is initialised with the depression of the full draft.

X 210.title: Prescribed constant linear velocities of the floating body in [m/s]
X 210.text: Applied to the degrees of freedom set to 2 in X 11, ramped with X 206.

X 211.title: Prescribed constant angular velocities of the floating body in [rad/s]
X 211.text: Applied to the degrees of freedom set to 2 in X 11, ramped with X 206.

X 240.title: Read motion file for 6DOF motions

options.1: Translation format: t, x, y, z
options.11: Course over Ground format: t, x, y, CoG (acts on u, v and r)
options.21: Piston wavemaker format: t, x (acts on u)

X 240.text: The motion is read from 6DOF_motion.dat; the velocities are computed from the differences between consecutive lines and applied to the degrees of freedom set to 2 in X 11 (ramped with X 206). CoG = course over ground (yaw angle) in [deg].

X 241.title: Time shift for motion files in [s]
X 241.text: Added to the time column of 6DOF_motion.dat (X 240) and of the piston wavemaker.dat (X 170).
