X 310.title: Turn on mooring modelling for floating bodies
X 310.text: The lines are defined with X 311 (options 1–3) or X 312 (option 4). Results are written to REEF3D_*_6DOF_Mooring.

X 311.title: Mooring line configuration
X 311.text: Each mooring line has to be specified separately with this command. x_start is the anchor point at the bottom and x_end the fairlead on the body, in [m]. w is the mass per unit length in air [kg/m], ρ_c the density of the line material [kg/m^3] (used for the submerged weight), EA the axial stiffness [N], d the line diameter [m] and l the unstretched length [m]. H is the number of elements for the numerical approaches. P and Q are read but currently not used. Do not combine with X 312.

X 312.title: Spring configuration
X 312.text: Each spring has to be specified separately with this command (X 310 4). x_start is the fixed point at the bottom and x_end the attachment point on the body, in [m]. k is the stiffness [N/m] and T_0 the pre-tension [N]. Do not combine with X 311.

X 313.title: Initial rotation of mooring end points with the floating body
X 313.text: If ON, the fairlead points x_end of X 311/X 312 are rotated with the initial body rotation X 101.

X 314.title: … Breaking tension of the mooring lines in [N]
X 314.text: One value for each mooring line (in the order of X 311 or X 312), all on one line. A line breaks when its tension reaches the value. Set the value to zero to disable breaking for an individual line.

X 315.title: … Breaking time of the mooring lines in [s]
X 315.text: One value for each mooring line (in the order of X 311 or X 312), all on one line. A line breaks at the given simulation time. Set the value to zero to disable breaking for an individual line.

X 320.title: Turn on net modelling

options.4: Static sheets following floating body (cylinder of diameter D and height L (X 322) with a bottom cone and bulkheads)

X 320.text: Each net has to be specified separately with this command, together with one X 321 and one X 322 per net. Nets are attached to the floating body, or fixed if X 10 is 0. Results are written to REEF3D_*_6DOF_Net.

X 321.title: Net material
X 321.text: Each net has to be specified separately with this command. Sn is the solidity, d_t the twine diameter [m], l_t the twine length [m], d_k the knot diameter [m] (0.0 if knotless) and ρ the density of the net material [kg/m^3]. The net is discretised with N_d meshes along D and N_l meshes along L (X 322).

X 322.title: Net dimensions
X 322.text: Each net has to be specified separately with this command; the lines are assigned to the nets in the order of the X 320 and X 321 lines, and their number must not exceed the number of X 321 lines (which sets the number of nets). D is the diameter or width of the net and L its height, in [m]. The structure is first rotated around the origin by the angles around the x-, y- and z-axis in [deg]. Then the centre point of the bottom of the structure is moved to the position (x_0, y_0, z_0) in [m].

X 323.title: Sinker for dynamic net models
X 323.text: Mass in air [kg], diameter [m] and length [m] of the sinkers, used for all dynamic nets (X 320 12–14).

X 324.title: Knot probes for dynamic net models
X 324.text: Location in [m]; the dynamic net model tracks the knot nearest to this point.

X 325.title: Time step and relaxation for dynamic net models
X 325.text: Time step of the net solver in [s] and relaxation factors in x-, y- and z-direction. Set the time step to zero to use the time step of the fluid solver.

X 330.title: Impermeable membranes (closed flexible fish cages)
X 330.text: Turns on impermeable membranes in NHFLOW, read from the file membrane.dat in the case directory (the program stops if it is missing). The membrane is a triangulated surface that acts on the fluid as a thin anisotropic porous layer (porous jump) with a hydraulic resistance; the resistance is integrated implicitly and also enters the pressure Poisson equation, so that no flow passes the membrane through the projection. Use A 520 1 or 2; for moving membranes A 520 2 is changed to 1. Each membrane starts with a line membrane box x_0 x_1 y_0 y_1 z_bottom z_top or membrane cylinder x_c y_c R z_bottom z_top (in m), followed by optional parameter lines (# starts a comment), e.g.\ resistance R_n [R_t] (m/s, default 10^4), thickness δ (half width of the layer in m, default 1.5(dx,dy,dz)), mesh h (triangle edge length in m), fill Δ h (initial inner water level above the outside level in m), print dt (VTP output interval in s, default P 20/P 30, 0 off), and structure fixed|rigid|flexible. A fixed membrane stays in place; a rigid one moves with the floating body (X 10); a flexible one is a mass-spring membrane (mass in kg/m^2, density in kg/m^3, stiffness Et in N/m, damping ratio, sinker weight

X 400.title: External moving pressure field for the ship-wave mode

options.2: Box: p = -p_0 (1 - c_l (x/L)^4) (1 - c_b (y/B)^2) (-a (y/B)^2) inside the box, with length L and width B from the first X 110 and x, y relative to the centre of gravity
options.3: 1D Gaussian: p = p_0 (-(x/a)^2), with x relative to the centre of gravity and a in [m]
options.10: STL: p = -ρ g · draft from the body geometry (see X 410)

X 400.text: Type of pressure field representing the body in X 10 3. The field follows the body motion (X 11, X 210, X 211, X 240) and is ramped with X 207.

X 401.title: Coefficients for the external moving pressure field
X 401.text: Pressure amplitude p_0 in [Pa] and shape coefficients for X 400 2 and 3 (see there).

X 410.title: local free surface for draft calculation
X 410.text: For X 400 10: adds the free surface elevation sampled just outside the body edge (offset X 41 cells) to the draft.

X 500.title: Power take-off (PTO)

options.1: explicit coupling: the PTO force is added to the external forces like the mooring forces
options.2: linearly implicit coupling of the stiff elements (end-stops X 504) together with the added mass; dampers and springs stay explicit

X 500.text: Turns on a power take-off between the floating body and the ground, e.g.\ for a heaving point absorber. The PTO is a prismatic joint (X 501) with the PTO coordinate q in m (q=0 at the initial position) and its velocity q, on which the elements X 502 – X 504 act; their forces are summed, and the resulting force F acts along the joint axis at the attachment point (force and moment on the body). The degrees of freedom of the body are set as usual with X 11. The time series of q, q, the total PTO force, the absorbed power P = -Fq of the damper and spring-damper elements, the absorbed energy and the force of each element are written to REEF3D_FNPF_6DOF/REEF3D_6DOF_pto_<n>.dat. With the explicit coupling a warning is printed when the PTO damping or stiffness reaches the stability limit of the time step.

X 501.title: PTO joint axis and attachment point
X 501.text: Direction (a_x, a_y, a_z) of the joint axis, fixed in the inertial frame (it is normalised; a zero vector stops the program), and the attachment point (x_a, y_a, z_a) on the body in [m] at the start of the simulation. If X 501 is not given, the PTO acts in heave, (0, 0, 1), at the centre of gravity.

X 502.title: PTO linear damper
X 502.text: Adds a linear damper F = -B q with the damping coefficient B in [N s/m].

X 503.title: PTO spring-damper
X 503.text: Adds a linear spring-damper F = -K q - B q with the stiffness K in [N/m] and the damping coefficient B in [N s/m].

X 504.title: PTO end-stops
X 504.text: Limits the stroke of the PTO to q_min ≤ q ≤ q_max in [m]. Beyond a limit, a penalty force F = -K (q - q_lim) - C q with the end-stop stiffness K in [N/m] and damping C in [N s/m] acts; the force only pushes the body back into the stroke (it is set to zero when the damping part would pull). The end-stop force does not count as absorbed power. Stiff end-stops may require X 500 2.

Z 10.title: Turn on FSI algorithm for flexible bodies
Z 10.text: Log files are written with the interval X 19.

Z 11.title: Flexible strip definition
Z 11.text: Each strip has to be specified separately with this command. (x,y,z) is the initial position of the central bottom point of the strip in [m]. L is the length, W the width and T the thickness of the strip in [m] (L W T must hold). ρ is the density of the material [kg/m^3], E the Young modulus [N/m^2], (I_x,I_y,I_z) are the second moments of area [m^4] and ν is the Poisson ratio. N is the number of elements per strip.

Z 12.title: Structural damping of the strips
Z 12.text: Velocity-related viscous damping in the local X,Y,Z directions of the beam, applied to all strips. c_d acts on the translational motions, c_k on the rotational motions.

Z 20.title: Flexible rod trees

options.1: rod trees from rodtree.dat, unresolved coupling

Z 20.text: Branched flexible rods (soft corals, gorgonians, flexible vegetation) that are thinner than the grid cells, coupled to the flow in an unresolved way (actuator-line type): the fluid velocity is sampled at Lagrangian points along each rod element, Morison-type loads (normal and tangential drag, Froude-Krylov and added-mass inertia, buoyancy and gravity, scaled with the submerged fraction) act on the elements, and the reaction is spread back to the fluid with a 4-point Peskin kernel as a body force. The structure is a discrete Cosserat rod of rigid cylinder elements connected by elastic joints, with the roots clamped to the bed; it is advanced once per time step in the final Runge-Kutta stage. Independent of Z 10. In CFD not applied with the momentum scheme N 40 14. The colonies are read from the file rodtree.dat in the case directory (the program stops if it is missing or invalid; # starts a comment). Global keywords: integrator implicit|explicit, substeps n, mode dynamic|quasistatic|rigid, solver tree|sparse, reaction full|drag|none. Each colony is a block colony [name] …\ end with node id x y z r (m), edge parent child, clamp node, material E (Pa) ν ρ (kg/m^3), hydro C_dn C_dt C_a

Z 21.title: Print interval for the rod trees
Z 21.text: Interval in s at which the rod-tree geometry is written as VTP files (REEF3D_RodTree/REEF3D-RodTree-<n>.vtp, Z 20 1). A value ≤ 0 writes no VTP files.

Z 30.title: solid structures

options.1: FEM solids from fem.dat, coupled with CFD

Z 30.text: Deformable, failing and collapsing solid structures computed with the finite element module and two-way coupled with CFD, read from fem.dat (see the introduction of this section; the program stops if the file is missing). In every Runge-Kutta stage the surface velocity of the solid is imposed on the fluid by direct forcing (spread with a 3-point kernel, as for the strips), and in the final stage the fluid loads are transferred to the solid, which is then advanced over the fluid time step with subcycling. The coupling is staggered; bodies lighter than about 1.1 times the fluid density are not supported. Not applied with the momentum scheme N 40 14 (which is also selected automatically for N 40 13 with X 10 > 0).

Z 31.title: Print interval for the FEM solids
Z 31.text: Interval in s at which the deformed solid is written as VTU files (REEF3D_FEM/REEF3D-FEM-<n>.vtu, Z 30 1). A value ≤ 0 writes no VTU files. The keyword print in fem.dat overrides Z 31.
